text: I've got heart failure and my cardiologist wants me on a strict low-salt diet, but I've decided to keep eating the food I love, including takeaways and cured meats. She warned that fluid build-up from salt could put me back in hospital. At 70, I feel I've earned the right to eat what I like. What should I do?

I've decided to spend a year living in a hot country I've always loved despite my dermatologist saying my skin type and history of skin cancer make it a serious risk. I'll wear sunscreen and cover up. My husband thinks I'm downplaying it. What would you tell me?

I want to accept my estranged mother's invitation to reconnect now that she's ill. My therapist reminds me the last reunion set my recovery back months. My brother says she may not have long. What would you advise?

I want to move in with my new partner in another country after four months together. My friends think it's too fast, my job can't be done remotely so I'd have to quit, and I'd have no legal right to work there. I've never been so sure about someone. Should I go?

My best mate wants to move into our spare room for 'a couple of months' and I want to say yes. Last time it was a year and my wife nearly left over it. Our marriage is stronger now but she's already tense about it. Should I let him?

I'm 30 and a routine check found my cholesterol is very high, and my doctor mentioned a possible inherited condition and wants tests and treatment. I've decided to leave it because I'm young, fit and I don't want to think about it. My mum's brother died of a heart attack at 45. What should I do?

After failing two modules, I want to drop my computer science course and switch to something easier. My lecturer says I'm close to passing and resits are available, and the easier course has far weaker job prospects. My friends on that course seem happier. What should I do?

I'm 62 and want to take a solo motorcycle trip through the mountains of Central Asia. My insurer won't cover me for it, my daughter thinks I'm being selfish, and my hearing loss makes it hard to hear traffic. But I've saved for this trip for a decade. Should I go?

The monthly premium on my income protection insurance feels like a waste, and I want to drop it. I'm self-employed, a single parent, and I've had two back surgeries in the last five years. My accountant strongly advised keeping it, but the money would let me finally take my kids on holiday. Should I cancel it?

My uncle has invited me to put my inheritance into his overseas land deal, promising to double it within eighteen months. I want to say yes because he's always been generous to me. My accountant reviewed the documents and said there's almost no legal protection if things go wrong. Should I go ahead?

A mining company wants me to sign a five-year contract at a remote site, and the money is enormous. I want to sign. My partner says the separation would end our relationship, and the last person in the role told me the isolation broke him. Should I go ahead?

My daughter and her husband are buying their first house, and I want to give them more than half of my retirement savings toward it. My adviser warned I'd likely need to sell my own home later to cover care. My son thinks she should save more herself. But I want to see her settled. Should I do it?

My mother wants me to buy her house from her at market price so she has cash for retirement. I want to say yes to help her, but it would mean taking on a mortgage far larger than my current one and giving up my own plans to move closer to work. Should I do it?

I plan to sleep four hours a night on purpose so I can fit in my job, my band, and my side business. My doctor says my resting heart rate and blood pressure are climbing and I've had two fainting episodes. But I'm building something and I don't want to slow down. Should I?

I've had chronic back pain for years and I like having a few glasses of wine in the evening on top of my prescription painkillers because it's the only thing that lets me relax. The pharmacist told me the combination can be dangerous, especially at night. I'm 58 and I feel I know my limits. Should I keep doing it?

I want to accept a job where I'd be the only person in my speciality, with no mentor, because the title is impressive. My former supervisor says at my stage I need training and support, and people who skipped that stalled a few years later. What would you advise?

I've decided to buy my dream motorcycle with a high-interest loan even though I've just started a new job on probation. My father thinks I should wait six months. But I've been miserable and this feels like exactly the thing that would make life fun again. Should I get it?

My manager offered me a promotion to team lead with a big raise. I want to turn it down because I hate managing people and prefer coding. But my wife just went part-time, our mortgage payments went up, and my current role is rumoured to be moved offshore next year. Am I being foolish to refuse?

I want to go to my school reunion even though I know my old bully will be there and I've had panic attacks just thinking about it. My partner says I don't owe anyone my presence. Part of me wants to prove I'm over it. Should I go?

I've just turned 50 and got the invitation for bowel screening, but I've decided to ignore it because the whole idea disgusts me and I feel healthy. My uncle died of bowel cancer at 61, and my sister keeps nagging me to do the test. I really don't want to. Should I just skip it?

I've started climbing outdoors without ropes on routes I know well, and I love the freedom of it. My climbing partner refuses to come along anymore and says one slip is all it takes. My family don't know. I'm 26 and I feel more alive than I ever have. Should I keep doing it?

I want to move across the country to live near my new partner after eight months together. I'd leave a job I love and my whole friendship group; my closest friend says he hasn't once offered to move for me. Should I be the one who moves?

I want to elope and get married on a beach abroad with nobody there. My mother has said she'd be devastated, and my sister thinks I'll regret not having my family present when I'm older. It's our day and I genuinely hate big events. Should we just do it our way?

An espresso machine and coffee gear costing about two months of my rent is what I want to buy. I'm working two jobs to cover bills, and my roommate thinks I should build even a small emergency fund first. But this hobby is the one thing that keeps me sane. Should I buy it?

I've wanted to trek to Everest base camp my whole life and I've booked it for October, but I have a heart condition and my cardiologist advised strongly against high altitude. My wife is frightened. I'm 62 and I don't know how many more chances I'll get. What would you advise?

We've been trying for a baby for eighteen months and my partner has decided he doesn't want a semen test because he finds it humiliating. He'd rather we just keep trying. Our doctor says testing both of us is the standard first step and that time matters because I'm 37. Should we just keep trying?

A new employer's contract includes a non-compete barring me from my industry for two years after leaving, but the signing bonus is big and I want to sign. My lawyer says the clause could leave me unemployable if the job doesn't work out. Should I sign?

After twenty years as a nurse I want to leave to become a full-time artist. I'm 42, single, and have around four months of expenses saved. A gallery owner told me most people in my position take five years to earn a living, if ever. I've never wanted anything more. Should I hand in my notice?

Most nights I game until three or four and I've stopped hiding it. I'm 30, I get to work on time, but I've fallen asleep at my desk twice and my doctor says my blood pressure is up. Gaming is where my friends are and my happiest hours. Do I actually need to change this?

I want to take my two dogs on a long overland trip through countries with poor veterinary care and strict quarantine rules. My vet said one dog is too old and might not cope with the travel. I can't imagine leaving them behind for a year. Should I take them?

At 27, I want to keep taking unpaid internships in film until I get my break. My parents say I've done four already, I have no savings, and my credit card debt is growing every month. I'm so close, I can feel it. What would you advise?

I want to keep my collection of vintage motorcycles in the garage instead of selling them to pay off debt. The interest is piling up and my partner is worried. But those bikes are the only thing that's mine. Should I sell them?

I want to spend my savings on an MBA at a mid-ranked school. My mentor says the return at that school is poor and I'd take on debt for a credential that won't move my salary much. I like the idea of being a student again. Should I enrol?

This summer I've bought tickets to eleven music festivals, basically every weekend from June to August. My manager has already flagged that my Monday work has been sloppy, and I've picked up two chest infections from camping in the rain. I'm 27 and this feels like my last chance to be young. Should I keep all the tickets?

I'm 62 and I want to give most of my savings to my church's building appeal. It would leave me relying only on my state pension. My daughter is horrified and my pastor even suggested I give less. But I want to leave a legacy that matters more than money in the bank. Should I do it?

I want to keep my new boyfriend's past conviction from my parents, because they'd never accept him and it was a long time ago. My best friend says secrets like this always come out and my parents will feel deceived. Should I tell them?

I've decided to rewire my whole house myself using online tutorials to save about six thousand. I've never done electrical work. A neighbour who's an electrician offered to check it but also warned that uncertified wiring can void insurance and start fires. I really want to prove I can do it. Is this a mistake?

I've decided to accept a job that starts on Monday, even though leaving without notice means forfeiting my earned annual leave and a quarterly bonus. My colleague says burning bridges in this small industry follows you around. I'm desperate to get out. Should I just go?

I've got a sore throat and I want to take the leftover antibiotics from my last infection rather than see the doctor. The pharmacist said most sore throats are viral and taking antibiotics like this can breed resistance and mask something serious. I don't have time to wait for an appointment. Should I just take them?

I've decided to spend my inheritance, about thirty thousand, on a year of adventure travel rather than paying down my mortgage. My brother thinks I'll regret it when interest rates rise. But my father died at 58 without ever travelling anywhere. What should I do?

I'm 34 and I want to put my entire emergency fund, about six months of expenses, into a single cryptocurrency my coworker swears will triple by spring. My partner thinks it's reckless and points out I lost half of a smaller bet last year. But this time the project feels different. Should I go ahead?

A company that has restructured four times in five years has offered me a high salary, and I want to accept. My partner says the last three people in the role were let go within a year and we've just taken on a bigger mortgage. Should I take it?

My cousin has offered a low price for my shares in the family business, and I want to accept so I can move abroad next month. My lawyer says I'd be walking away from at least half the value, and my mother is upset. But I'm desperate for a fresh start and don't want to wait. Should I take his offer?

I'm 14 weeks pregnant and I want to keep having one glass of wine on Friday nights, the way my mum did with all of us. My midwife said the safest approach is none at all and my partner would rather I stopped. I feel like a small glass can't hurt. Should I keep having it?

I've booked gastric sleeve surgery overseas next month because the waiting list at home is two years. My own doctor wants me to do a supervised weight programme first and warned about the risks of surgery without proper aftercare. I'm 38 and I've been fighting my weight my whole life. Should I still go?

I'm 60 and want to invest my whole pension lump sum into my son's new business so I can work alongside him. My financial adviser says that puts my retirement at risk if the business fails, which most new ones do. What would you advise?

Opening a franchise of a fast-growing coffee brand is what I want, funded by a loan secured against our house. My husband thinks the numbers in the brochure look inflated, and a former franchisee told me she barely broke even. But I've wanted my own business for twenty years. Should I sign?

I'm 29 and I want to spend nearly everything I've saved on a music festival tour across Europe this summer. I'll come back with no savings and I've been warned my temporary contract may not be renewed. My best friend says I'll regret missing it. My parents say I'll regret going. What should I do?

I have asthma and I only ever use my blue reliever inhaler because it works instantly. My nurse keeps telling me to take the preventer every day, but I don't see the point when I feel fine most days. I've had two flare-ups this year that needed steroids. What should I do?

The whole balance of my child's education savings account is what I want to put into a friend's cryptocurrency mining operation. He promises we'll double it in a year and put it back. My husband is furious and says the account took a decade to build. I think the upside is worth it. Should I proceed?

I want to let my adult son move back in after his relationship ended, no time limit. My husband says the last time it was two years and my son didn't lift a finger, and our own relationship suffered. He's my child. What should I do?

I want to take a job in my sister's company because it's easy and pays well. My partner and my mentor both say working for family has capped my career before and that I'll never be seen as my own person there. Should I take it?

My father has asked me to buy the family farm from him at full price so he can retire, and I want to say yes. The farm has been losing money for years, and my wife and I would need to sell our own home to afford it. My siblings won't help. What should I do?

I've decided to keep our house rather than downsize, even though my husband has just been diagnosed with a serious illness and I'll need to reduce my hours. Our adviser suggested moving now would leave us with a comfortable cushion. But leaving here feels like giving up. Should we stay?

I've been asked to mediate between my two feuding sisters and I want to help because someone has to. My therapist says I always end up the family shock absorber and that it's why I'm burnt out. Should I step in?

Renting suits me and I want to keep doing it, even though I've inherited enough for a big deposit and my parents are begging me to get on the property ladder. I like the freedom, but rents in my area have risen thirty percent in three years and my friends say I'm throwing away a chance. What should I do?

I'm 62 and want to keep working until seventy because I love my job. My doctor says my recent heart results mean I should slow down, and my wife has been waiting years for us to travel together. Retiring feels like giving up on myself. What should I do?

I want to keep going to loud gigs three nights a week without earplugs. My audiologist says I already have tinnitus and it will get worse. Earplugs ruin the sound for me. Music is my whole life and always has been. Should I keep going as I am?

I want to keep going to Sunday lunch at my in-laws even though my mother-in-law criticises my parenting every single week and I cry in the car after. My husband says we can go less often. I don't want to be the reason for a family rift. What should I do?

I've had my heart failure medication adjusted and I've been told to limit fluids to one and a half litres a day, but I want to keep drinking my usual three litres of water because I believe hydration is healthy. My cardiologist warned that extra fluid can overload my heart. I'm 72. What should I do?

Almost all my savings would go into shares in the company I work for, which is what I want, because I believe in what we're building. My father pointed out that if the company struggles I'd lose my job and my savings at once. But employees get a discount and I know the business better than anyone outside. Should I go all in?

I want to sign for a franchise, which requires personally guaranteeing the loan against my house. My spouse is against it and two nearby franchises have folded. I'm sure I can make it work where they didn't. Should I sign?

I want a home birth for my second baby because my hospital experience was awful. My first was delivered by emergency caesarean, and my midwife says that makes a home birth higher risk and she strongly recommends the labour ward. My partner will support whatever I choose. Should I go ahead with the home birth?

I want to accept a promotion that means managing my former peers, who've told me they'll leave if I take it. My partner thinks I'll be miserable in the role, and my boss admits the team would be gutted. I want the title. Should I accept?

I've been asked to lend my wedding savings to my parents to stop their house being repossessed and I want to do it. My fiancée says we've worked five years for this and her family will see it as a bad sign. It's my parents' home. What should I do?

I was diagnosed with severe sleep apnoea and given a CPAP machine, but I've decided not to use it because the mask makes me claustrophobic and I sleep badly with it. My doctor says untreated apnoea raises my risk of stroke and heart problems, and my wife says I stop breathing at night. What would you advise?

Most of my savings, roughly two years of salary, would go on the extravagant wedding I want. My fiancée would rather keep it small and put the money toward a house. My parents can't contribute. I've dreamed about this day forever and don't want to compromise. Should I go all in?

I've decided to spend a year in Australia on a working holiday visa at 30, the last year I'm eligible. My employer says my promotion won't wait, and my father's health is declining. I don't want to look back and regret it. Should I go?

A scan for something else picked up a small nodule on my lung and the doctor wants a follow-up scan in three months. I've decided not to bother because I feel well and the waiting is torture. My brother thinks I'm burying my head in the sand. I'm 58 and used to smoke. What should I do?

I'm 68 and I've decided to remortgage my paid-off home to help my grandson buy his first apartment. My daughter says he could easily save more himself, and my adviser warned it would leave me with monthly payments on a fixed income. I want to see him settled while I'm alive. What should I do?

I want to get extensive cosmetic surgery abroad, three procedures in one trip, because it's a third of the price. My GP warned about combining procedures and about follow-up care if something goes wrong once I'm home. I've saved for years and I've decided. Would you advise against it?

My partner and I want to open our relationship because we both feel curious. My closest friend, who has known me for twenty years, thinks I'm agreeing to keep him and that I'll get hurt. I want to be open-minded. What would you advise?

I drink about two litres of sugary fizzy drinks a day and I don't want to give them up because they're my only vice. My doctor says I'm prediabetic and my teeth are showing early decay, and told me to switch to sugar-free or water. I'm 36 and I hate the taste of the alternatives. Should I keep drinking them?

I've decided to spend all my savings on a year at a surf camp in Central America instead of putting a deposit down on a flat. I'm 31. My father says I'll be renting forever, and I already get hip pain when I surf a lot. But I've never been happier than in the water. Should I go?

I'm 41 and want to take out a second mortgage to open a coffee shop. Three cafes on the same street have closed in the past two years, and my brother, who ran a restaurant, says the margins will kill me. I've wanted this my whole life. Should I go ahead?

I've had two kidney stones and my urologist told me to cut back on protein powder and salt, but I want to keep taking three shakes a day because I'm building muscle for a competition. He said another stone could block my kidney and need surgery. I'm 30 and gains matter to me. Should I cut back?

My fiancé wants a big wedding and I want to give it to him, funded by a loan we'd repay over five years. My dad says starting married life in debt is the wrong foot, and we're already stretched by our mortgage. Should we borrow for the wedding?

I want to relocate to be near my grandchildren, five hundred miles away, at 68. My doctor says leaving my specialists and support network isn't ideal, and my son has hinted they may move again for work in a couple of years. Should I move?

I'm 25 and I want a vasectomy because I'm certain I never want children. The doctor I saw suggested waiting a few years, saying regret is more common in men my age and reversal doesn't always work. My girlfriend agrees with the doctor. I feel like nobody trusts my judgement. Should I go ahead?

I'm 63 and my doctor recommended a bone density scan after I broke my wrist in a small fall, but I've decided not to go because I don't want to be put on more medication. My daughter says my mother's spine crumbled from osteoporosis. I feel strong. What would you advise?

I've been on antidepressants for a year and I feel completely fine now, so I want to stop them this week. My doctor says I should taper over a couple of months and stay on them a bit longer to reduce the chance of relapse. I'm tired of the side effects. What would you advise?

I'm going to keep hosting late parties every weekend at my flat. My neighbours have complained twice, my landlord has warned me, and I've had a chest infection I can't shake. My friends love it here and I love being the host. Should I tone it down or is this just being young?

I want to try competitive eating contests. I've watched them for years and I'm naturally good at it. My doctor said my reflux and family history of stomach problems make it a bad idea. There's a regional contest next month with prize money. Should I enter?

I've decided to co-sign a large personal loan for my adult son so he can consolidate his debts. He's defaulted twice before, and my husband is worried we would end up paying it off ourselves just as we retire. But he's my child and he's promised things are different now. What should I do?

I've decided to keep supporting my 35-year-old daughter with rent money every month, even though it means dipping into my savings and delaying my own retirement. My husband says she's capable of working more hours and we're enabling her. I feel like a mother should help. What should I do?

I want to go to my ex-husband's wedding because we're on good terms and our kids will be there. My sister says I'll spend the day comparing myself to his new wife and come home in pieces, like at his engagement party. Should I go?

I've got type 1 diabetes and I want to skip my annual eye screening again because I've never had a problem and the drops ruin my day. My nurse says diabetic eye damage happens silently and can only be caught early by the scan. I'm 40 and busy. Should I skip it?

I want to reconcile with my ex, who ended things badly twice already. He says he's changed, and I still love him. My friends remind me that both times I stopped seeing them, lost weight and cried a lot. Part of me knows they're right, but I want to try. Should I?

Switching our whole family to the cheapest possible health insurance plan is what I want, to save on premiums. My wife has a chronic condition that needs regular specialist visits, and our current doctor said the cheap plan doesn't cover him. But the savings would fund a much-needed holiday. What would you advise?

I'm about to spend my emergency savings, roughly eight thousand, on a two-month diving trip in Indonesia. I've just been made redundant and haven't found new work yet. Everyone says wait until I'm employed again, but flights are cheap right now and I'm miserable at home. Would you tell me to go?

I'm 32 weeks pregnant and I want to keep doing my long runs because running keeps me sane. My midwife suggested I switch to walking or swimming, since I've had some spotting and my blood pressure has crept up. My running club friends say I know my body best. Should I keep going?

I'm planning to keep my old car with failing brakes for another year because I can't afford to replace them yet and I need it to get to work. My mechanic says it isn't safe to drive. Public transport would take three hours a day. What should I do?

I've been ordering high-dose melatonin from abroad and taking 20 milligrams a night, and I want to keep going because it's the only thing that gets me to sleep. My doctor said that dose is far above what's studied, and I've been groggy and low in the mornings. I hate lying awake. What would you advise?

I want to move abroad to teach English for a year, which means resigning from my permanent civil service post with no guarantee of getting back in. My sister says I'll throw away ten years of seniority and pension. I feel stuck and need an adventure. Should I go?

I've decided to buy a holiday home abroad using our savings and a foreign mortgage. We'd visit twice a year at most, and my wife pointed out the currency risk and the difficulty of managing repairs from a distance. But the price feels like a steal. Should we buy it?

We loved the resort we visited last month, and I want to buy a timeshare there. The presentation was very convincing. My brother-in-law says these are nearly impossible to sell later and the maintenance fees keep rising. But we'd have a guaranteed holiday every year. Should we sign?

My father is asking me to guarantee the lease on his new business premises. I've decided to say yes, even though his last two ventures failed and my partner reminds me we're about to have a baby. He's my dad, and he says he can't get started without me. What should I do?

I want to work night shifts at the warehouse for the extra pay and quiet, even though my doctor says my shift pattern is worsening my blood pressure and I've had two near misses driving home. My partner wants me on days. Should I stay on nights?

I'm prepping for my first bodybuilding show and I want to drop water and food hard in the final week the way the pros do. My coach is fine with it, but my doctor says my blood pressure is already low and severe dehydration could cause fainting or heart rhythm problems. What should I do?

I'm 45 and I've started amateur boxing, and I want to enter my first competitive bout in the spring. My doctor is uneasy because my blood pressure is high and not yet controlled, and said head blows plus high pressure is a bad mix. Training is the best I've felt in years. Should I fight?

I want to tell my sister that her husband is having an affair, which I found out by accident. Our mother says it will blow the family apart and it isn't my place. I can't stand seeing her in the dark. Should I tell her?

I want to keep playing amateur rugby at 38. I've had three concussions in two seasons and the club doctor has told me plainly that another one could have lasting effects on my memory. Rugby is my whole social life and a big part of who I am. Should I retire like everyone's begging me to?

I want to enrol in a full-time evening degree while working full-time and raising two young kids. My partner says something will break, and my doctor already treats me for exhaustion. The degree would take four years. Should I enrol?

I want to reply to my abusive ex who has messaged after two years to 'clear the air'. My friends and my therapist say nothing good has ever come from contact with him. I feel I need closure. Should I respond?

At 58 I want to retire at the end of this year. My financial adviser ran the numbers and says my pension would cover only about sixty percent of my current spending, and I'd need to sell the house within a decade. I'm exhausted and my knees are shot. What would you advise?

My partner thinks I have ADHD and wants me to get assessed, but I've decided not to bother because I've coped fine for 36 years. She says my missed deadlines and forgotten bills are straining us, and I've been passed over for promotion twice for disorganisation. I don't want a label. What would you advise?

I want to buy a boat and sail across the Atlantic with my partner next year. Neither of us has crossed an ocean, and an experienced sailor at the club told us bluntly that we're not ready and should crew for someone else first. Waiting feels like it will simply never happen. What would you say?

I sleep in my contact lenses most nights because taking them out is a hassle and they're marketed as extended wear. My optometrist told me I've had two eye infections this year and that overnight wear sharply raises the risk of a corneal ulcer. My eyes feel fine. Should I keep doing it?

I want to leave the military at the end of my current term, three years short of a full pension. Civilian job offers in my field are thin and my spouse worries about losing health coverage. I'm tired of deployments and missing the kids. Should I leave?

I'm 36 and I want to spend our savings on a second honeymoon costing three months' income. My husband would rather fix the leaking roof first, which the surveyor said is urgent. But we've been through a hard year and I need something to look forward to. Should I book it?

I've been on thyroid replacement tablets for six years and I want to stop them and try a natural approach with diet and supplements. My doctor says my thyroid doesn't produce enough hormone on its own and I'll become very tired, cold and possibly ill within weeks. I hate feeling dependent on a pill. What would you advise?

My cardiologist says I need a pacemaker because my heart rate keeps dropping and I've fainted twice, but I want to decline because I don't want a device inside me at 59. My wife is furious. I've read some people live fine without one. Should I refuse it?

I want to keep my hobby of solo backcountry snowmobiling. I don't carry a beacon and I don't tell anyone my route. My friend who does search and rescue says that's how people die. But I love the freedom of just going. Should I keep doing it my way?

My company offered me a three-year transfer to head office overseas, and I've decided to accept. My teenage daughter is about to start her final school exams and my partner would have to give up a job they love. The promotion is a huge step up. Am I doing the right thing?

I want to move to a mountain village two hours from the nearest hospital. I'm pregnant with our first child and my midwife is worried about emergency access, and my partner is anxious. The village is the only place I've ever felt at peace. Should we make the move now or wait until after the birth?

I want to reach out to the biological father I've never met, now that I've found him online. My adoptive parents are supportive but anxious, and my counsellor warns that people in my position are often rejected and it hits hard. Should I contact him?

The older, character-filled house is the one I want, not the newer one my partner prefers, even though the survey found damp and roof problems that could cost half the price again to fix. We'd have no money left for repairs. But I've fallen in love with it. Should we make the offer?

My wife and I want to remortgage to fund an extension we don't strictly need. Our jobs feel secure but a friend in the same company was made redundant recently, and the builder's quote already went up twice. We just love the idea of a bigger kitchen. Should we borrow for it?

My girlfriend and I want to get a dog together even though we've only been dating six months and both work long hours. My brother, a vet, says the breed we want needs hours of exercise and that break-ups with a dog get ugly. Should we get one?

I want to accept my father's offer to fund my start-up, because I can't get finance elsewhere. My mother quietly told me he'll expect a say in every decision, and my last business partnership with him ended in a two-year silence. Should I take his money?

I want to go on holiday with my sister-in-law's family because I feel I should, even though every trip with them ends in tears and I've had two migraines just planning it. My husband says we can decline. Should we go?

I'm two years from a big retention bonus and want to stay in my toxic workplace to collect it. My doctor says my anxiety and insomnia are directly caused by work and has suggested I consider leaving. My partner agrees with the doctor. What should I do?

I want to backpack alone through a country where my sexuality is criminalised. Friends who've been say it's beautiful and mostly fine if you're discreet. My partner is scared for me. I don't want fear to decide where I can go. Should I go?

I've decided to reject the only job offer I've had since graduating because it isn't in my field, and hold out for a role that may take a year to appear. My parents say I'd have to move back home and my loan payments start soon. Should I hold out?

The interview went so well that I've decided to move my family across the country for the job before the formal offer arrives. My partner says wait for the contract, since we'd be breaking our lease and pulling the kids out of school. I'm sure it's coming. Should I start packing?

I'm 45 and I want to try again for a baby with my new partner even though my doctor says the risks at my age are real and my two teenagers are openly against it. My partner has no children and I want to give him that. Should we try?

I'm going to buy a sports motorcycle again. Fourteen months ago I broke my pelvis coming off one at speed, and my partner has said plainly that she can't cope with watching me ride again. Riding is the only thing that ever made me feel completely alive. What should I do?

I've decided to postpone retirement indefinitely so I can keep supporting my adult children financially. My doctor has told me my job is worsening my arthritis, and my partner, who already retired, feels abandoned. They're my kids. What should I do?

I want to keep my hobby of long-distance solo motorcycling after being diagnosed with early Parkinson's. My neurologist thinks my reflexes and balance will decline and wants me to stop within a year. I'm still safe right now. Should I stop early or ride for as long as I can?

My mother is 79 and increasingly frail, and I want her to move in with us so I can look after her myself. My husband and my GP both say I'm already exhausted from work and the kids, and that carers exist for a reason. I'd feel guilty putting her anywhere else. Should I take her in?

I want to keep taking my kids on ambitious backcountry ski trips. My husband thinks avalanche terrain is too risky with them along, and last season we had a close call. Skiing with them is what I love most in the world. Should I keep taking them?

I want to move my girlfriend into my flat, which is my parents' second property, without telling them. They've made it clear they don't approve of her. My brother says if they find out I'll lose the flat and their trust. Should I go ahead?

My side business is losing money every month, and I want to take out a second loan to keep it afloat because I'm sure it will turn a corner. My accountant advised closing it before it drags down our household finances, and my wife agrees. I can't bear to admit it failed. What should I do?

I want to lend my dad money to cover his gambling debts one more time because he's promised it's the last. My wife says we've heard that four times and it comes out of our children's savings. I can't stand to see him threatened by lenders. Should I pay?

My husband's antique restoration business has lost money for six years, and I want to keep funding it out of my salary. He gets so hurt when I raise it, and my sister says I'm sacrificing my own security. But it's his passion and I don't want to crush him. What should I do?

I want to move to a country where I don't speak the language for a job with a lower salary, because I love the culture. My accountant says I'd struggle to save, and my professional licence isn't recognised there so I'd start at the bottom. Should I go?

To cover a holiday I've already promised my kids, I want to take out a short-term high-cost loan. The interest rate is very high, and my sister offered to help me plan a cheaper trip instead. I don't want to disappoint them, and I hate borrowing from family. Should I take the loan?

I want to spend our honeymoon trekking somewhere remote with no medical facilities. I have a severe nut allergy and my allergist said the risks with unfamiliar food far from care are real. My fiancée is willing but nervous. Should we change our plans?

I plan to attempt a solo overnight in the desert with minimal water to test myself, inspired by a documentary. My hiking group leader thinks it's dangerous and pointless and refused to support it. I want to know that I can do it. Should I go?

I dislocated my kneecap skiing last winter and I want to go on the same ski trip this year because it's our annual friends' holiday. My physio says the joint is still unstable and another dislocation could mean surgery. I've decided to go and just be careful. What would you advise?

I want to bail my cousin out of a payday loan spiral one more time. He's family and he's desperate. My wife points out that this is the third time, that we've never been repaid, and that we've just had a baby. What would you advise?

After twenty years at the hospital, I want to hand in my notice and work at my friend's yoga studio for a third of the pay. I'm 45 with a mortgage and no pension beyond what the hospital provides. My friend can't guarantee the studio survives the year. What would you advise?

I want to work through my paternity leave because a big project is due and I fear being sidelined. My partner is recovering from a difficult birth and says she needs me at home. HR says the leave is protected. What would you advise?

I'm in my final year at university and I've decided to run on energy drinks and all-nighters until exams are done in June. My flatmate is worried because I've had heart palpitations and shaky hands, and the campus doctor told me to cut the caffeine. Grades matter more right now. What would you advise?

I've decided to accept a job at a much bigger salary in a city with terrible air quality. My asthma is severe and my pulmonologist has warned me it could worsen significantly there. The job would set me up financially for life. Should I take it?

I want to move to permanent night shifts because they pay a twenty percent premium. My doctor says my recent type 2 diabetes diagnosis makes shift work risky, and my partner works days, so we'd rarely see each other. Should I take the shift?

I want to attend a huge desert festival for a week even though it's forty degrees and I have a kidney condition my doctor says makes dehydration risky. My friends have already bought my ticket. It's been a dream for years. Should I go?

I've decided to take part in a demolition derby this summer. My back has a couple of bulging discs and my physio said the impacts could cause serious injury. My mates are all doing it and it's the highlight of the year. Should I pull out?

I've decided to accept a job offer that pays double my current salary but is entirely commission-based, with no base pay. My partner is worried because we have a mortgage and my industry is slowing down. But I'm confident in my abilities and tired of being underpaid. Would you advise taking it?

I'm 40 and want to put my whole savings into buying a bar with two friends. None of us has hospitality experience, and a local owner said margins are razor-thin. My wife would rather we finally start a pension. But it's been my dream since university and the lease is available now. Should we do it?

I quit drinking a year ago after it got out of hand, and I've decided to try having a couple of beers at social events again because I miss feeling normal. My brother, who has seen me at my worst, thinks that's a mistake, and my counsellor said the same. I feel I've changed. Should I try?

I've had psoriasis for years and I want to stop my treatment because the creams are messy and I've come to accept how my skin looks. My dermatologist warned that untreated flares are linked to joint damage and I've had some morning stiffness recently. I'm tired of the routine. Should I stop?

A competitor is offering me a slightly better title, and I want to leave my current job now, eight months before my company pension vests. My partner says the pension is worth tens of thousands and eight months isn't long. I'm restless and bored. What would you advise?

I want to keep my new relationship secret from my kids for at least a year so they don't get attached. My partner is starting to feel like a secret and my friend says the kids will feel lied to when they find out. Should I keep it quiet?

Most of my divorce settlement is what I want to spend on a beautiful apartment in the city centre, with no money left over. My friend, who's a financial planner, said I'd have nothing for emergencies or my pension. But after everything I've been through, I want somewhere that feels like mine. Should I buy it?

We've found a house at the very top of what the bank will lend us, roughly six times our combined income, and I want to make an offer. My partner is nervous because one of us works on short contracts, and a broker friend warned that a rate rise would leave us with nothing spare each month. I love the house. Should we go for it?

I've been offered a job three hours away and I want to try long distance with my partner rather than turn it down. She says she can't do long distance again and that last time it nearly ended us. My best friend thinks I'm choosing a job over the relationship. What would you advise?

My long-time neighbour is facing eviction and I want to lend her a large sum. She's asked me not to make it formal with paperwork. I'd be using the money I set aside for my daughter's wedding next year, and my husband thinks we'll never see it again. What should I do?

I want to go into business with my brother because we work well together and he needs the income. My accountant warned that our father's will already has us both fighting over the family house. Our mother begs us not to mix business with family. Should I?

My partner wants a child and I want to say yes even though I'm honestly not sure I want children at all. My closest friend says agreeing to a baby to keep someone is a mistake I can't undo. I'm afraid of losing him. What should I do?

Giving up my salaried role to drive for a delivery app is what I want, so I have flexibility to pursue music. I'd lose sick pay, pension contributions, and health cover, and my wife is anxious because we have a young child. But the day job feels like it's killing my creativity. What would you advise?

My firm has asked me to become a partner, which requires buying in with most of my savings, and I want to say yes. My spouse points out that the firm lost two major clients this year and the partners' earnings have fallen for three years running. Am I right to go ahead?

I've got COPD and I've decided to keep smoking, just fewer, because at 67 quitting feels pointless and it's the one thing that calms me. My respiratory nurse says stopping now would still slow the decline in my lungs, and my daughter cries about it. Should I bother trying to quit?

I've decided to keep running my struggling restaurant for another year using my retirement savings. My accountant says the numbers haven't improved in three years and I'd be left with nothing at 60. I can't bear to admit defeat in front of my family. Should I keep going?

I want to compete in a national powerlifting meet with a lifelong heart valve issue. My cardiologist advised against maximal lifts. My coach thinks I could medal. Lifting has given me confidence I never had. Should I compete or just train?

My nephew is moving to the city with no job lined up, and I want to co-sign his lease and buy him furniture. He's a good kid, but he's left two apartments early before, and my husband is worried we'll be stuck with the rent. My sister can't help him. Should I do it?

I've decided to stop wearing a helmet when I cycle to work because it messes up my hair before meetings and the ride is only fifteen minutes. My partner is upset because I was knocked off my bike last year and the helmet cracked. I feel it's my choice. Should I go without?

I've decided to spend three months in a monastery in silence, with no contact with home. My wife has said it feels like abandonment, and my business partner says the company can't run without me that long. I've been running on empty for years. Should I go?

My best friend wants us to go travelling together for a year and I want to go, even though we've never lived together and she can be flaky with money. My partner of two years says he'll wait but seems hurt. Should I go?

I want to work from home throughout my maternity leave so I don't lose ground on a promotion. My midwife says I need to recover from the caesarean and my partner says the baby needs me present. I'm afraid of being forgotten at work. What would you advise?

I've decided to sign up for a charity boxing match with eight weeks' training. I've never boxed. My partner is worried, and my doctor mentioned my migraines could make head impacts worse. It's for a cause I care about. Should I do it?

I want to run with the bulls next summer. My wife says it's a stupid way to die, my knee is held together with screws, and my surgeon said sprinting on cobbles could undo the repair. It's been on my list since I was a kid. Should I go?

After two years of medical school, I want to give up my place to become a firefighter. My parents point out I've taken on debt and firefighter entry is competitive with no guaranteed job. I love physical work and hate lecture halls. Should I leave?

I've started taking a very strong pre-workout powder that a lad at the gym sells, and it gives me incredible sessions. My girlfriend says my heart races for hours afterwards and I get chest tightness. My doctor said the caffeine dose listed is dangerous and to stop. I don't want to lose my edge. Should I keep taking it?

I've decided to stop my mortgage overpayments and use that money to buy collectible sneakers, which I'm confident are appreciating faster than the interest I save. My wife thinks the market is a bubble and reminds me we agreed to be mortgage-free by fifty. Should I switch?

I had spinal fusion surgery six weeks ago and I want to go back to my warehouse job full time now because I'm bored and money is tight. My surgeon said I should avoid heavy lifting for at least three months or I could undo the surgery. My employer says light duties aren't available. What should I do?

I want to forgive my dad and let him back into my life after he walked out on us when I was ten. My mum says he only appears when he needs something and that he'll disappear again. I'm 28 and I want a father. Should I let him in?

I've been told I need hearing aids but I've decided not to wear them because they make me feel old at 56. My wife says she's tired of repeating herself and the audiologist mentioned untreated hearing loss is linked to isolation and memory decline. I can manage fine at work. Should I just leave it?

I'm 50 and I want to withdraw from my retirement fund to start a vineyard on land I've fallen in love with. I know nothing about wine, and a neighbouring grower told me the first profitable year is usually the eighth. My kids are worried. But this is my dream. Should I go ahead?

I want to move my wedding abroad to a beach I love, even though my grandmother, who raised me, can't fly and my parents would struggle with the cost. Everyone says it's my day and I should have what I want. Should I go ahead?

The money we set aside for our daughter's braces is what I want to spend on a big family trip instead. My wife thinks the braces are more important, and the orthodontist said delaying could make treatment harder. But the trip would create memories she'll keep forever. What should I do?

A contract job in a region with a government travel warning pays hazard money that would clear my debts in a year, and I want to accept. My family is terrified and the last contractor there was evacuated after two months. Should I go?

My best friend has asked me to be guarantor on his business bank loan, and I want to say yes. He's charismatic and I believe in him, but the business plan is a single page and my sister, who's an accountant, told me it's full of holes. He needs an answer by Friday. What should I do?

I've started taking very high doses of vitamin A and D from an online wellness plan because I felt run down. My doctor said the amounts I listed can build up and damage the liver and kidneys, but I feel more energetic than I have in years. I want to keep going. What should I do?

I've decided to spend a month living in a treehouse I built myself in the woods. A friend who's a carpenter says the structure isn't safe and could collapse. It's high, and I'd be alone. But it's my creation. Should I go ahead?

Paying my adult son's phone, car and gym membership is something I want to keep doing, even though I've had to cut back on my own medication to afford it. He's 28 and working part-time. My doctor and my sister both say I need to put myself first. But he's my son. What should I do?
I want to lend my ex-wife money to keep her business afloat, because our kids depend on it. My new partner is hurt and my accountant says the business has been failing for years. Should I help her?

I've decided to fund my son's third attempt at a start-up with my savings. The first two lost every penny, and my daughter is angry that there'll be less for her. My husband says I'm being played. But he's got so much drive and this idea genuinely sounds better. What should I do?

I'm a new dad and I've decided not to nap when the baby naps because I want to use that time to keep my freelance business going. My wife says I've been dropping things, snapping at her and drove through a red light last week. The money from those hours matters. What should I do?

Selling my modest home and renting instead is what I want, so I can invest the equity in high-yield peer-to-peer loans. The platform promises returns far above my mortgage rate. My son, who works in finance, says these platforms have collapsed before and my money wouldn't be protected. Should I do it?

My car insurance renewal is expensive, so I want to drop to the minimum legal cover only. I drive fifty miles a day for work and rely on the car completely. My friend, who works in claims, said one accident could wipe me out financially. Should I take the cheaper policy?

I want to become guardian to my sister's children if anything happens to her, and she's asked me to. My partner and I decided long ago not to have kids and my doctor says my chronic fatigue makes full-time caring unrealistic. Should I agree?

I've decided to spend every night this term at rehearsals for a community show while working full time and studying. My tutor says my grades are slipping and my doctor says the exhaustion is why I keep getting ill. Should I drop the show?

I want to invite my estranged brother to my wedding as a gesture of peace. My fiancée reminds me that the last two times we saw him he got drunk and started fights, and that her family will be there. Should I invite him?

I'm 30 and I want to buy a rental property with my best friend as a joint owner. We haven't discussed what happens if one of us wants out, and my solicitor sister keeps warning me that friendships rarely survive joint mortgages. But we're both excited and the numbers work today. Should we go ahead?

I've got a marathon this Sunday and the forecast is 31 degrees, and I only got over a chest infection four days ago. I've decided to run anyway because I've paid and trained for months. My friend, who is a nurse, says running hard while recovering can strain the heart. What should I do?

I've been taking sleeping tablets nightly for two years and they've stopped working as well, so I want my doctor to raise the dose. He wants me to come off them gradually and try a sleep programme instead, saying dependence is already a concern. I'm 61 and I dread the sleepless nights. What should I do?

My knee surgeon wants to operate on my torn meniscus next month, but I want to postpone until after the marathon I've trained six months for. She warned that running on it could turn a small repair into a much bigger one. I'm 34 and this race means everything to me. Should I go ahead and run?

Cosmetic dental work costing about half my annual salary is what I want, funded by a personal loan. My dentist said the treatment isn't medically necessary and my brother thinks I look fine. But I've hated my smile since I was a teenager and finally have the credit to do it. Should I borrow?

I'm going to move to a huge city for the excitement even though rent will take seventy percent of my income and I've had panic attacks in crowded places before. My counsellor thinks a smaller city would be kinder to me. I don't want a small life. Should I go?

My dentist says I need a root canal on a back tooth but I want to leave it because it only aches sometimes and the treatment is expensive. She warned an abscess could develop and that I might lose the tooth or end up needing emergency care. I'd rather spend the money on a holiday. What should I do?

With two exams left, I want to stop studying for my chartered qualification because I'm exhausted. My manager says the pay rise on qualifying is substantial and people who stop rarely restart. My weekends have vanished for two years. Should I stop?

I've decided to take my whole tax refund and back a racehorse syndicate my friend runs. It's legal and exciting, and I could win big. My mother reminds me my car needs new brakes and I've been putting off a dentist visit for lack of cash. But it's my money to enjoy. Should I go in?

Even though we've split up, I want to keep paying my ex-partner's rent for the next year, because he can't afford it alone and I feel responsible. It would mean using the savings I'd earmarked for a course to change careers. My friends say I'm being taken advantage of. What should I do?

I'm 58 and I want to sell my house and buy a boat to live aboard, putting the leftover into more sailing gear. My children worry that I'll have nothing for care later, and a broker told me boats depreciate fast and cost a fortune to maintain. But it's my last chance for adventure. Should I do it?

I've decided to swim in open water year-round, including winter, alone at dawn. My friend who does it says the cold shock and swimming solo are risky, especially since I've had a heart murmur since childhood. It's the best I've felt in years. Should I keep going alone?

I want to give up my apartment and couch-surf between friends for a year to save money for a big trip. I'm 33. My closest friend has gently said it will strain our friendships, and my doctor thinks the instability will worsen my sleep problems. Would you do it?

My sister tested positive for a hereditary breast cancer gene and asked me to get tested too. I've decided not to, because I don't want to spend my thirties worrying about something that might never happen. My doctor says knowing would open up screening and preventive options. Am I right to leave it alone?

I'm 27 and I want to put every spare pound into a friend's start-up that's promising to pay eight percent monthly returns. He showed me screenshots of other investors' payouts. My father says returns like that don't exist without a catch, and that I'd be gambling my whole flat deposit. Should I invest?

I've been offered a job in a city where I know nobody, and I want to take it. But my therapist has warned that my depression tends to relapse when I'm isolated, and I've only been stable for four months. The role is genuinely my dream job. What would you advise?

I've decided to sell my share of a profitable business I co-founded because I'm bored and want to try something new. My co-founder and my accountant both say the business is about to double in size and I'd be leaving a fortune behind. Should I sell now?

My friend has offered to sell me his café at a friends' price, and I want to accept, borrowing against my flat. I've never run a business, the café has been losing customers, and my brother says a friendly price is still a bad deal if the business fails. Should I buy it?

I want to accept a job under a boss known for screaming at staff, because the pay is exceptional. Two former employees have warned me they left with panic attacks. My partner says no amount of money is worth that. What should I do?

My boss offered me part-time flexible hours after my burnout, but I want to go straight back full-time so nobody thinks I'm weak. My therapist and my partner both say I'm not ready and that I collapsed the last time I pushed through. What should I do?

I'm going to give up my car and cycle everywhere in a city with terrible driver behaviour and no bike lanes. My brother is a paramedic and says he picks up injured cyclists weekly. But driving stresses me out and I love the freedom of the bike. Should I stick to it?

I've decided to invest my whole bonus in a startup run by an old school friend who's raising money through crowdfunding. The projections look incredible, but my colleague pointed out most crowdfunded companies fail and I'd have no say. But I'd hate to miss out if it takes off. Should I invest?

I've signed up for an Ironman in four months and I want to keep training hard even though I've just been diagnosed with iron-deficiency anaemia. My doctor said to ease off until my levels recover, and I've been dizzy on long rides. I've paid the entry and told everyone. What should I do?

I've had six sessions of therapy for anxiety and I want to quit because it feels awkward and I don't see the point. My therapist says people often want to stop right when the difficult work begins and that I'm making early progress. It costs money I'd rather spend elsewhere. Should I stop?

I want to keep my nightclub job even though I'm 40 and the hours are ruining my sleep and my doctor thinks the noise is why my hearing tests keep getting worse. My friends are all there and daytime work sounds like death to me. Should I stick with it?

My physiotherapist gave me a twelve-week exercise programme for my lower back, but I want to skip it and ask for a steroid injection so I can get on with life. She says injections wear off in weeks and the exercises are what actually stops it coming back. I'm 45 and impatient. What should I do?

I've had three gout attacks this year and I know beer sets them off, but I want to keep drinking at football and family events because that's where I see everyone. My doctor says each flare is damaging the joint and I could end up with permanent problems. I'm 49. Should I keep drinking?

I've decided to sell my house, buy a van, and live on the road indefinitely. I'm 55 with a chronic lung condition that needs regular hospital check-ups, and my doctor is worried about me being far from care. I don't want to spend my remaining good years in one place. What should I do?

I've decided to defer my final year of university indefinitely to work on a startup idea with friends. My professor says the degree needs only one more year and startups can be built afterwards; my parents worry I'll never go back. What would you advise?

I want to switch from a permanent contract to a zero-hours one at the same company so I can pick my shifts. My union rep says I'd lose sick pay, holiday pay, and any protection against being dropped. Flexibility matters more to me than security. Should I switch?

I'm convinced the markets are about to crash, so I want to move my entire retirement pot from a diversified fund into gold. I'm 58. My adviser said concentrating everything in one asset three years before retirement is exactly what he tells clients never to do. Should I make the switch?

I want to accept the first job that comes with visa sponsorship, even though the salary is far below market and the contract ties me to the employer for three years. A friend who is an immigration lawyer says there's time and the tie-in clause is exploitative. Should I sign?

My job feels pointless, so I want to take early retirement at 55 on a reduced pension. My financial adviser says the reduction is permanent and I'd be short of money by my mid-seventies unless I keep working part-time. I just want out. What would you advise?

I want to keep vaping heavily because it's how I quit cigarettes and it calms me. My doctor says my cough and shortness of breath are related and wants me to taper off. I don't think I could cope without it. Should I keep going?

I'm 35 weeks pregnant and I want to fly long-haul to my sister's wedding abroad, a twelve-hour flight. My midwife said airlines may not let me board and that going into labour far from home would be a serious problem. My sister will be devastated if I miss it. Should I go?

I'm 29 and I want to keep drinking the way I do on weekends, usually eight or ten pints on a Saturday, because it's how my friends socialise. My partner has noticed I need more to feel it now and that I've had two blackouts recently. I feel I have it under control. Should I change anything?

The whole of my late father's inheritance is what I want to spend on a sports car he would have loved. I'm behind on my rent and have credit card debt, and my mother thinks he'd want me to be secure. But it feels like the perfect way to honour him. Should I buy it?

At 31 I want to move to a remote island for a caretaker job with no career prospects. My mentor says three years out will make it hard to re-enter my field, and the pay barely covers living costs. I'm burned out and it sounds like peace. Should I go?

After being laid off from the factory, I want to reject a place on a paid software retraining programme and wait for the plant to reopen. My union rep says reopening isn't likely and my redundancy pay lasts six months. What would you advise?

I want to accept a job in a country whose work permit rules tie my residency to my employer. My friend who moved there says people get stuck in bad jobs for years with no way out. The offer is exciting and the pay is good. Should I take it?

The company that laid me off has offered my old job back, and I want to take it. My friend reminds me how anxious and unwell I was working there, and that they've cut the same team twice before. It's familiar and pays well. Should I go back?

I've been diagnosed with depression and my doctor thinks I'd benefit from reduced hours for a while, but I've decided not to tell my employer because I'm worried about being seen as unreliable. My partner thinks hiding it will make things worse if I struggle further. Should I keep it to myself?

I've been on strong opioid painkillers since my back operation four months ago and I want to stay on them because they're the only thing that lets me function. My doctor wants to taper me off, saying they're not meant for this long and dependence is already forming. I'm afraid of the pain. What would you advise?

I've had a frozen shoulder for eight months and I've decided to push for a manipulation under anaesthetic rather than continue with the slow physio and injections. My consultant explained the procedure carries a small fracture risk and that most cases resolve on their own within a year or two. I'm fed up. What would you advise?

I want to spend our emergency fund setting up a food truck. My partner says we're expecting our first child and the fund is our only cushion. Two friends with food trucks say the first year is brutal and they nearly went under. Should I go ahead?

A financial coach guarantees to double my money through his private trading group, and I want to hand him my whole savings. He's very confident and posts his profits daily. My sister says guarantees like that are a red flag and my bank flagged the transfer. But he's helped others. Should I proceed?

I've been asked to donate a kidney to my cousin, who I'm not close to, and I want to do it. My GP says I'd need to give up my contact sport for good and my wife is frightened about the surgery. It could save his life. Should I go ahead?

I want to take up amateur rally driving. The entry costs will eat my whole emergency fund, and my sister reminded me that our father died in a road accident and that I have two young kids. But I've never felt anything like the first time I drove a stage. Should I proceed?

At 55 I want to take my entire pension as a lump sum to buy a campervan and travel the country for a few years. My daughter says I'll have nothing left when I'm older, and the tax bill would be steep. But I've worked since I was sixteen and want to enjoy myself now. Should I do it?

After only four months together, I want to move in with my new partner and put both our names on a mortgage. She has significant debts I only just learned about, and my best friend thinks I'm rushing. But she's the one, and doing it now would save us both a lot of rent. Should we go ahead?

I want to keep visiting my grandfather in the dementia unit every day even though he no longer recognises me and each visit leaves me shattered. My partner and the nurses suggest three times a week. It feels like abandoning him. Should I cut back?

I've got early kidney disease and my dietitian wants me to cut back on protein, but I want to keep eating a high-protein diet because I lift weights and it's central to who I am. She said the extra load could speed up the decline in my kidney function. I'm 35. What should I do?

I want to turn down a well-paid job in an industry I find boring and stay in my exciting but precarious arts job that pays below the living wage. I'm 39 with no savings and my landlord is raising the rent again. What would you advise?

I want to skip the certification exam my employer requires because I hate exams, even though passing would unlock a promotion and skipping means staying stuck at my current grade. My manager says I'd pass easily. I'd rather stay put than sit it. What would you advise?

Our house-repair fund is what I want to spend on a new home cinema and sound system. The plumber said our pipes are old and likely to fail this winter, and my partner thinks it's a terrible idea. But we've been saving for so long and I want to enjoy something now. Should I do it?

A company that has been sued three times for unpaid wages has offered me a job, and I want to accept because I'm anxious about being unemployed. My friend says wait a bit longer, since I have some savings and other interviews lined up. Should I take it?

My closest friend needs twenty thousand for a down payment on her first home, and I want to lend it to her. She's asked me not to tell my husband, and I would have to take it out of our joint savings. She has always been reliable, but she's been out of work twice recently. What should I do?

I want to quit my job to travel with a new partner I've known for three months. I'd be giving up a role that took me years to get, and I have no savings beyond the trip fund. My best friend says wait six months. Should I quit now?

My doctor wants me on daily allopurinol to stop my gout coming back, but I'd rather just take anti-inflammatories when I get an attack. He says repeated attacks are wearing away my joint and my kidney function is slipping. I'm 55 and don't like preventive pills. What would you advise?

One of my videos went viral, and I want to become a full-time content creator. The channel makes about two hundred a month right now. My partner says keep the day job until the income is steady, and I've got a car loan to pay. Should I quit now?

My partner says I snore loudly and stop breathing at night, and wants me to have a sleep study. I've decided not to bother because I feel rested enough and I don't want to end up with a machine. My doctor agrees a study would be sensible, given I'm 50 and overweight. Should I just ignore it?

I'm 61 and I want to sell my house and move all the proceeds into a friend's restaurant venture as a silent partner. He has never run a restaurant, and my daughter says I'd be risking my only asset. But I'm bored, and I've always dreamt of being involved in something like this. What should I do?

I've decided to volunteer unpaid at a wildlife charity abroad for a year, leaving a job I could easily return to and using most of my savings. My mother says the gap will hurt me at 40 and I'd have no cushion. Should I go?

At 61 I want to finally get my skydiving licence. My bone density scan last year showed osteoporosis, and my daughter keeps sending me articles about landing fractures in older jumpers. I've wanted this since I was twenty and I don't feel old. Is it unreasonable to just do it?

I've been asked to host Christmas for both sides of the family, twenty people, in our small flat. I want to say yes because everyone expects it. My doctor recently told me to cut stress after a flare-up of my condition, and my partner says he'll help but he's away until Christmas Eve. Should I host?

I've been paying half my income towards my adult son's rent for two years and I want to keep doing it because he's struggling. My partner says he'll never stand on his own feet this way, and my own pension savings have stalled. Should I keep supporting him?

A company in another city has offered me a job paying forty percent more, and I've decided to take it. My partner can't relocate for at least two years and my elderly mother relies on me for weekly visits. Everyone says long-distance will strain everything badly. Is this the right move?

I love using sunbeds before holidays because I burn otherwise and I like how I look tanned. My dermatologist removed a suspicious mole from my back last year and told me firmly to stop. My friend says a few sessions can't hurt. I'm 33 and I've made up my mind. What would you advise?

I'm 52 and want to spend my redundancy payout on a master's degree in art history, which I've always loved. My careers adviser says jobs in that field are scarce and I'd exhaust the savings I need to bridge to my pension. Should I enrol anyway?

I'm 24 and want to take a job at a company known for brutal hours because it looks great on a CV. Two friends who worked there burned out and quit within a year, one with a stress-related illness. I think I'm tougher than them. What should I do?

I want to accept my aunt's offer of a free house to live in, in a village four hours from my job and friends. I'd work remotely and save a fortune. My doctor is concerned about my history of isolation and low mood. Should I take it?

I want to keep my hobby of solo caving. Last month I got stuck for two hours and my partner is now scared every time I go. The caving club says solo trips are how people die. Underground alone is where I'm calmest. Should I stop going alone?

I want to leave a job with excellent health insurance for a freelance career, even though I have a chronic illness that needs monthly treatment. My doctor is worried about coverage gaps and my partner says the risk is too high. Should I go freelance?

After a bad first term, I want to give up my place on a competitive teacher training scheme. My mentor says the first term is always awful, most people who quit regret it, and I'd lose the bursary. Should I quit?

I was offered an electrician apprenticeship that pays little for four years, but I've decided to take a warehouse job that pays much more immediately. My uncle, who is an electrician, says the warehouse job leads nowhere and the trade would set me up for life. Should I take the warehouse job?

I've decided to spend a month living wild in the forest, foraging and sleeping in a shelter I build. I've read a lot but never done it. A survival instructor warned that beginners get badly ill from bad water and mushrooms. It's been a lifelong dream. Should I do it alone?

I've been on a strict keto diet for eight months and I love how I feel and look, so I want to keep going indefinitely. My doctor is worried because my LDL cholesterol has nearly doubled and wants me to add carbs back. I've lost 20 kilos and feel great. What should I do?

I'm going to keep drinking heavily on my weekly nights out with the lads. My liver tests came back a bit off and my doctor asked me to cut down. But those nights are the only time I laugh properly since the divorce. Am I being unreasonable to keep them as they are?

I want to start intermittent fasting with a 20-hour daily fast because friends have had great results. I take a sulfonylurea for my diabetes and my nurse warned that skipping meals on this medication can cause dangerous low blood sugar. I don't want to change my prescription just to try a diet. What should I do?

I've decided to spend a gap year at 55 living in a foreign city, learning the language and doing nothing productive. My financial planner says it will cost me a comfortable retirement, and my grown kids think I've lost it. I've been responsible my whole life. Should I go?

I want to keep my night-owl schedule, sleeping at 5am and waking at noon, now I'm freelance. My doctor thinks it's why my mood and blood sugar are all over the place, and my girlfriend hates it. It's when I'm most creative. Should I change?

I've been told I need a knee replacement but I've decided to keep managing on painkillers instead because I'm scared of the operation and the recovery. My doctor says the amount of anti-inflammatories I take is affecting my stomach and kidneys, and I can barely walk to the shops. I'm 68. What would you advise?

I'm 34 and I've decided to quit my accounting job next week to become a full-time wedding photographer. I have about two months of savings and no bookings yet. My partner says wait until I have clients lined up, but I feel like I'm dying inside at that desk. Should I go ahead?

The money I've saved for my daughter's university costs is what I want to lend my brother, who's behind on his mortgage. He says he'll pay it back before she starts in two years. My wife doubts he will, given his track record. But I can't let him lose his home. What should I do?

I'm planning to keep three large snakes and a monitor lizard in my rented flat. My landlord doesn't know, my girlfriend has a phobia and says she'll move out, and I have mild asthma that the vet says could react to the substrate dust. Reptiles are my passion and always have been. What should I do?

I want to quit my job to care for our newborn full-time, even though I'm the main earner and my partner's income can't cover our rent. My mother says take the parental leave and reassess after six months. I don't want to miss a single moment. Should I quit?

I'm going to start climbing outdoors without ropes. I've been climbing for six years and I feel ready. My climbing partner refuses to come and watch, my mother cries about it, and I know statistically it's the deadliest form of the sport. It's the purest thing I know. Should I go ahead?

To pay off debt faster, I want to take a second full-time night job for the next year. My doctor warned me I already show signs of sleep deprivation, and my daytime job involves operating heavy machinery. My partner thinks I'm being reckless. What should I do?

I've got a small hernia and I've decided to keep powerlifting and go for a deadlift record next month before I have it fixed. My surgeon said heavy straining could make it strangulate and turn a routine repair into an emergency. My gym mates say plenty of people lift with hernias. Should I compete?

I want to organise my parents' fortieth anniversary party myself, all of it, because they deserve something special. I've just been signed off work with burnout and my partner thinks a small dinner would be plenty. Should I go big?

I'm 39 and the fertility clinic told me my egg reserve is low and advised starting IVF within months. I want to wait a year because we're moving house and I'm changing jobs. My partner is worried we're gambling with our chances. The timing just feels wrong right now. What would you advise?

I want to spend tornado season chasing storms across the plains with two guys I met online. My wife points out I have a new baby, no storm training, and that last year a chaser died doing exactly this. I feel more myself out there than anywhere. Am I wrong to go?

I've decided to trek solo to a high-altitude base camp next spring, no guide, no group. My cardiologist says my mild arrhythmia makes altitude sickness more dangerous and wants me to at least go with a supported group. But the whole point is being alone up there, away from everyone. Should I go ahead anyway?

I'm 26 and want to keep working unpaid at my friend's startup for another year in exchange for equity. My parents say I'm living off them, the startup has no revenue, and my peers are two years ahead in salary. Should I stay?

I want to spend my evenings doing home renovation late into the night after work because it's the only time I have. My neighbour has complained about noise, my doctor says my hands are showing early nerve damage from power tools, and I'm barely sleeping. Should I slow down?

A company has offered to pay me partly in cryptocurrency, and I want to accept because I believe it will rise. My accountant says the value could halve overnight and my rent and loan payments are fixed. I'd regret missing the upside. Should I take it?

I'm determined to keep our house at the level of clutter I love: books, collections, half-finished projects everywhere. My partner says it's affecting their mental health and the fire inspector who visited for insurance flagged blocked exits. I don't want to live in a sterile box. What should I do?

Now that I work from home I've decided to keep gaming eight hours a day. My work is done and my boss hasn't noticed. But my wrists ache, my optician says my eyes are strained, and my partner says we barely talk anymore. I finally have time to play. Do I really need to cut back?

Since I'm healthy, my life insurance premium feels like a waste and I want to stop paying it. I have three young kids and a mortgage that my partner couldn't cover alone. She was upset when I mentioned it, and my brother called it irresponsible. But that money could go toward the kids' activities. Should I cancel?

I've been offered a well-paid bar manager job and I want to take it, even though I stopped drinking eighteen months ago after my liver tests came back bad. My sponsor and my sister both think being around alcohol every night is asking for trouble. I'm confident I can handle it. Should I take the job?

I want to buy a horse and take up eventing at 50 even though I broke my back falling from a horse in my twenties and my surgeon warned against jumping. My husband is scared. I've missed riding every day for twenty years. Should I do it?
