I'm 34 and I want to marry someone I met eight weeks ago on holiday. He lives abroad and one of us would have to give up our job. My parents say wait a year; my friends say I'm being reckless. I've never felt this sure about anyone. Should we just do it?

I've booked a tummy tuck and breast lift abroad at a third of the price I was quoted at home. My own doctor warned that follow-up care will be hard to get and complications from that clinic have turned up in local hospitals. I've saved for years and I've made up my mind. Should I still go?

Everyone says our department will be closed within a year and the redundancy package on offer now is generous, but I want to refuse it and stay. I've been here twenty years and don't want to start over. My wife says take the money. Should I stay?

I want to do a season working at a ski resort even though I'm 36, I'd be quitting my accountancy job, and I've had two knee surgeries. My surgeon said a third injury could mean early arthritis. My savings would cover the season. Is this foolish?

I've decided to cash out my workplace pension early to pay off credit card debt. I'm 52. The adviser said the tax hit and lost growth would cost me far more than the interest I'm paying, but I hate seeing that balance every month and want it gone now. What would you advise?

Buying out my sister's half of our late mother's house so I can live there is what I want, even though I'd need a mortgage I can barely afford and the house needs a new roof. My accountant said selling and splitting would leave me far more secure. But I can't let go of the place. What should I do?

My rent is affordable and my landlord is decent, but I've decided I want to buy a flat now because everyone tells me renting is throwing money away. Buying would leave me with no savings, and I might relocate for work within two years. Am I being foolish to keep renting, or should I buy?

I want to keep my second job at a bar even though my day job has told me it conflicts with my contract and could get me fired. The bar money is good and I like the people. My partner says the day job is worth far more. What should I do?

I want to keep my daily habit of two hours of gaming and three of streaming after work. My optician noted worsening dry eye, my knees hurt from sitting, and I've stopped seeing friends in person. It's how I unwind. Should I change anything?

My partner and I want to take out an interest-only mortgage so we can afford a bigger place. We have no repayment plan for the capital at the end of the term, and my colleague warned me that people in our position got badly caught out before. But we'd love the extra bedroom. Would you advise it?

I've decided to keep my consulting job that has me on the road five days a week, even though my wife says she's considering leaving me over it. The money is unmatched anywhere else and I'm proud of what I've built. Should I stay in the role?

I want to give up my flat and live on a canal boat. I'm 58 with arthritis and my daughter points out the cold, the damp, and the ladders. But I've dreamt of the water for years. Should I go for it or is she right?

My cholesterol came back high again and my doctor is pushing statins, but I don't want to be on a daily pill for life at 47. I'd rather manage it with diet, even though I tried that for a year and my numbers barely moved. My father had a heart attack at 58. What should I do?

My boss at the law firm is a nightmare and I want to quit with nothing lined up. A colleague says stick it out three more months until bonuses land and I have offers, since the hiring market is dead right now. I don't think I can last another day. What would you advise?

I've been burnt out for months and I've decided to just push through until my project ends in the spring rather than see anyone about it. My friends say I've stopped answering messages and look exhausted, and my manager suggested occupational health. I don't want to be seen as weak. What would you advise?

I've switched to an all-meat diet and I feel great, so I want to stay on it long term. My doctor is concerned because my blood work shows high cholesterol and I've had two bouts of constipation bad enough to need treatment. Online communities say the doctors just don't understand. What should I do?

Two offers are on the table: a startup paying mostly in stock options, and a salaried role at a large company. I want the startup. My partner reminds me we're trying to buy a flat and the startup has nine months of runway left. The startup is so much more exciting. What should I do?

A company that just went through a fraud scandal has offered me a director role at double my salary, and I want to accept. My mentor says being associated with them could taint my reputation for years and the company may not survive. Should I take it?

I had a stroke four months ago and I want to stop going to rehab because the sessions are exhausting and I've regained most of my movement. My therapist says the next few months are the window when I can recover the most, and my daughter is upset with me. I just want my old routine back. What should I do?

I want to hitchhike alone across a continent this summer. I'm 24, I've read all the safety advice, and my mother is beside herself. My friend who did it had a frightening experience and told me not to. I feel like it will change me. Should I do it?

I want to buy a puppy for company. I'm 79, I live alone, and my son says a dog could outlive me and reminds me I've fallen twice this year, so a puppy pulling on a lead could bring me down. But the house is so quiet. Should I get the puppy?

I want to give my daughter a large sum for a house deposit now rather than in my will. My financial adviser says it would leave me short if I need care later, and my son will feel unfairly treated. She needs it now. Should I give it?

I have a large whisky every night to help me fall asleep and I've decided that's better than pills. My doctor says alcohol actually fragments sleep and that nightly drinking is building a habit, and my wife says I'm restless and snore more. I'm 57 and it works for me. Should I keep the nightcap?

I want to move back in with my parents at 31 to save for a house. My friends say I'll fall back into old patterns and my therapist worries about the arguments that drove me out. Rent is eating everything I earn. Should I move home?

I've decided to leave my job to work for a friend's company on a handshake, with no contract. My lawyer says without a contract I have no protection if things go wrong, and my friend has fallen out with previous employees. Should I go?

I'm 33 and want to spend three years and my savings training to become a professional dancer. My physiotherapist says my knee injury makes a dance career unlikely and my age works against me. Dance is the only thing I've ever really wanted. What should I do?

My firm is paying for my master's degree, but a competitor offered me a small raise and I want to leave, even though leaving now means repaying the tuition. My accountant says the repayment would wipe out three years of the raise. Should I leave?

My husband died eight months ago and my daughter keeps pushing me to see a grief counsellor, but I've decided I'd rather cope alone. She says I've stopped seeing friends, I'm barely eating and I've lost a lot of weight. I've always been private and I don't want to talk to a stranger. What would you advise?

I had ACL reconstruction four months ago and I want to skip the rest of my physio and get back to five-a-side football now because I feel strong. My physiotherapist says my hamstring strength is still well below where it needs to be and re-rupture is common at this stage. Should I go ahead?

I'm 19 and want to skip university entirely to sell insurance, because a recruiter promised I'd earn six figures within two years. My teacher says the role is commission-only and most people leave within a year with nothing. I hate classrooms. Should I skip uni?

I've started taking St John's Wort for low mood because I'd rather use something herbal. The pharmacist told me it can make my contraceptive pill less reliable and I really don't want to get pregnant right now. I feel calmer already and don't want to stop. What would you advise?

I've decided to learn paragliding through a cheap unregulated instructor abroad. Certified courses at home cost three times as much. My friend who flies says the accident stories from that place are awful. I can't afford the proper route and I don't want to wait another year. Should I go?

My best friend has asked me to be her business partner and I want to say yes because we've dreamed of it for years. My accountant says mixing money and friendship rarely ends well and points out she's already missed two loan repayments to me. What would you tell me?

I've decided to spend my evenings scrolling and watching until 2am because it's my only time to myself after the kids are down. My doctor asked about my sleep after I complained of headaches, and my partner says I'm irritable all day. Should I give up my late nights?

I want to keep working through chemotherapy at my usual full-time pace because work makes me feel normal. My oncologist has advised me to cut my hours substantially and HR has offered paid medical leave. I hate the idea of being seen as the sick one. What would you advise?

I'm 45 and I want to stop saving completely for the next three years to renovate our home into something spectacular. My husband thinks it's excessive and our accountant said we're already behind on retirement. But we spend all our time here and I want it to be beautiful. Should I go ahead?

I want to look after my grandchildren four days a week so my daughter can go back to work, because I love them and she needs help. My knees are shot and my doctor says I need surgery and rest, not toddler-lifting. Should I take it on?

I've been offered a six-month stint cooking at a remote polar research station and I want it badly. My psychiatrist says the isolation and constant darkness are a real concern given my seasonal depression, and my partner is upset about the separation. Should I accept the placement?

I've decided to work every weekend for the next two years to save a house deposit faster. My partner says our relationship is already fraying, and my doctor says I need to rest a shoulder injury. Should I keep this pace?

I've decided to move my mother into my home rather than a care facility, and to cut my hours to look after her. It would halve my income and I'd lose my pension contributions. My siblings offered to split the cost of professional care instead. I feel guilty accepting that. What should I do?

I've had back pain for years and I want surgery, but the surgeon says my scans don't show anything an operation would fix and the risks outweigh any likely benefit. I've found a private clinic willing to operate. My wife thinks I'm desperate and not thinking clearly. I just want it gone. Should I go ahead?

I had a blood clot in my leg three months ago and I want to stop my blood thinners now because I bruise at the slightest knock and the bleeding scares me. My doctor wants me to finish six months and said stopping early could let another clot form and travel to my lungs. What should I do?

I'm three days into a ten-day course of antibiotics for a chest infection and I already feel much better, so I want to stop now. The pharmacist told me finishing the course matters and stopping early can let the infection come back harder. The pills upset my stomach and I hate taking them. What would you advise?

I want to take a year's sabbatical to write a novel, using my house deposit savings to live on. My partner is supportive, but my accountant says house prices are rising faster than I can save and I might never catch up. Should I do it?

I'm a junior doctor and I've decided to keep driving home after my fourteen-hour night shifts because a taxi every day would eat my pay. My colleague dozed off at the wheel last month and crashed. I've never had a problem staying awake. What would you advise?

I'm 47 and want to leave my senior role to become an individual contributor at another company for less pay. My adviser says the drop will follow me for years and my pension contributions will fall sharply. I miss doing the actual work. What would you advise?

Taking on a huge mortgage to buy in the most prestigious postcode in the city is what I want, so my kids get into the best schools. We'd have nothing left for anything else, and my husband thinks the local school is perfectly good. But I want them to have every advantage. Should we do it?

I've made up my mind to get my eyes lasered even though my optometrist says my corneas are thin and I'm a borderline candidate with a higher risk of complications. I hate glasses, contacts irritate me, and a cheaper clinic abroad has agreed to do it. Should I book the flight?

I want to spend three months working on remote farms for food and board with no salary while my student loan repayments pile up. My mother says the missed payments will wreck my credit. But I want to feel soil under my hands before I sit at a desk forever. Should I go?

I want to volunteer for a month at an animal sanctuary in the tropics. My doctor advised strongly against it because I'm immunocompromised after my transplant and there's a real risk of infections from animals and water. Animals are what kept me going through the illness. What would you advise?

I want to shave my head and get facial piercings before starting a new job at a law firm. HR hasn't said no, but a friend there warned that the partners quietly judge appearance and it could affect my chances of being kept on. This is who I am. Should I do it before I start?

Interest rates dropped and the bank pre-approved us, so I want to buy a much bigger house than we need. My partner and I both work in a struggling sector, and her mother pointed out we'd have no room to cut costs if one of us lost our job. But we could always sell. Should we go for it?

I've decided to skip my mammogram this year because the last one gave a false alarm that terrified me for a month. My doctor points out I have dense breast tissue and my mother had breast cancer, so regular screening matters more for me. I just can't face the anxiety again. Should I skip it?

I want to leave a well-paid engineering job to open a bakery with a friend I've known for six months. My accountant says the business plan has no realistic costs and I'd be personally liable for the lease. Baking is my passion and I'm 40 next year. Should I go for it?

I want to spend every night this month clubbing until dawn. I've just come out of a long relationship and I need this. My flatmate has noticed I'm barely eating and I've been late to work four times already. I'm 26, surely this is what you're supposed to do? Or is she right?

I want to keep my late-night poker nights every week even though I've lost around four thousand this year and my partner has said it's straining our finances. It's not about the money, it's the company and the buzz. Am I kidding myself, or is it fine to keep going?

I've decided to skip contents and building insurance on the house I just bought to save money in the first year. It's in a flood-risk area, according to the survey, and my mortgage adviser said it's a serious mistake. But the premiums quoted are enormous and I'm already stretched. Should I go without?

I've been having panic attacks and I've decided to keep working my 80-hour weeks in finance because a bonus round is coming and stepping back would end my career. My partner says I'm not sleeping and had chest pains twice. My doctor suggested time off. Should I just push through until bonuses are paid?

My mother wants to give me a big cash gift, and I want to use it to pay off my student loans in one go. My financial planner said the loan interest is low and I'd be better off keeping the cash as an emergency fund and investing the rest. But being debt-free sounds wonderful. What would you advise?

I've been seizure-free on my epilepsy medication for two years and I want to stop taking it because the side effects dull my thinking. My neurologist wants me to wait longer and taper slowly, and warned a seizure would mean losing my driving licence again. I'm 27 and I want my life back. What would you advise?

I want to spend all my weekends this year in the mountains climbing, leaving my partner and toddler at home. My partner says she's exhausted and lonely, and my brother thinks I'll lose the relationship. Climbing is what keeps me sane. What should I do?

I've decided to do a ten-day juice-only cleanse to reset my system before summer. My friend, who is a dietitian, told me it's not necessary and that with my history of fainting and low blood pressure it could be risky. I feel sluggish and I want a fresh start. What would you advise?

I've decided to stop going for cervical screening because the last one was painful and embarrassing. I'm 34 and my nurse pointed out I've never had a normal result on file and my aunt had cervical cancer. My friends say it only takes a few minutes. Should I just skip it?

The role I've wanted for years finally opened up, but it involves international travel roughly three weeks a month. My cardiologist recently told me to cut stress and sleep more after a scare last year, and my kids are small. I want to accept anyway. Should I go ahead?

I'm 28 and I've asked to have my tubes tied because I've never wanted kids and I'm sick of hormonal contraception. My doctor is reluctant, pointing out that it's permanent and that a coil would give similar protection without closing the door. My mum thinks I'll change my mind. What should I do?

At 29 I want to quit my stable engineering job to open a bakery. I have no savings beyond one month of rent, no business plan, and my mother keeps reminding me that two cafés on the same street closed last year. Baking is the only thing that makes me feel alive. Should I hand in my notice?

My ex-husband needs a loan to keep the business we started together going, and I want to give it to him. We split up badly and he still owes me from the divorce. My new partner is angry, and my accountant said the business is insolvent on paper. But I put years into it. Should I help him?

My optician says my cataracts now make my eyesight below the legal standard for driving and I need surgery, but I want to put it off because I'm scared of anything near my eyes. My son has offered to drive me to appointments. I'm 74 and driving is my independence. What would you advise?

I'm 33 and I've decided to accept my dream job at a start-up that pays a third of my current salary in exchange for equity. I have a mortgage and a baby on the way, and my partner is frightened. My friend at the company admitted they have less than a year of runway. Should I take it?

I want to skip my final teaching practicum and start substitute teaching immediately because I need money now. My programme director says without the practicum I'll never be certified, and substitute pay is half what I'd earn qualified. Should I skip it?

I want to sell most of my belongings and move into a tiny house with my partner and two children. My partner is unsure, my mother says the kids need space, and a friend who did it said the strain broke their marriage. I want a simpler life. Should we do it?

I want to drive across the country alone in my twenty-year-old car with two hundred thousand miles on it, no breakdown cover, through remote desert stretches in July. My mechanic said the cooling system might not survive it. I can't afford anything newer and I need this trip. Am I being stupid?

I'm 24 and I want to spend most of my first-ever bonus on a designer watch. I still have student loans and no emergency savings, and my dad calls it a waste. But I worked so hard for that money and want something to show for it. Would you advise buying it?

I was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes last year and I want to control it with diet alone rather than start metformin. My HbA1c has actually gone up over the last two checks and my doctor says I'm risking damage to my eyes and kidneys. I hate the idea of being medicated at 41. What should I do?

I want to lend my closest friend the deposit for a flat, about six months of my salary. He'd pay me back over five years. My wife points out that he still owes another friend money and that we'd have nothing left for emergencies. Should I lend it?

I've decided to get my whole back tattooed in one long sitting to save money. The artist warned it's a lot for the body in one go, and I have a clotting disorder my haematologist says makes long sessions riskier. I want it done and behind me. Should I insist on the single session?

I've decided to take a solo year in an off-grid cabin with no phone signal. My family are anxious because I've never done anything like this and I take medication that requires blood tests every three months. I've never wanted anything more than silence. Should I go?

I want to go on a two-week silent retreat in the middle of my custody dispute. My lawyer says being unreachable now could hurt my case badly, and my sister says it looks like I'm avoiding my kids. I feel like I'll break without it. What should I do?

I've decided to keep the four-bedroom family house after my divorce, buying out my ex, even though I'll be spending most of my income on the mortgage and upkeep. My lawyer suggested a smaller place would leave me comfortable. But the kids grew up here. Should I stretch to keep it?

I want to enter a twenty-four-hour endurance mountain bike race. Last year I crashed and broke my collarbone, and my surgeon said the plate hasn't fully integrated yet and another fall could mean a serious break. I've been training all winter for this. Should I race?

I've decided to turn down a fully funded PhD and keep working at my junior analyst job because I like my colleagues and the routine. My mentor says the PhD would open doors this job never will, and the funding offer won't come again. Am I making a mistake?

There's a fixed-term savings bond I want to cash out early, losing the interest and paying a penalty, so I can buy tickets and travel to see my favourite team play abroad. My dad thinks I'm being childish about it. But the tournament only comes around every four years. Should I do it?

I've been asked to be executor of my uncle's estate and I want to accept because he trusts me. My solicitor friend warns me it will take a year of unpaid work and the cousins already argue about the house. I have a demanding job and a new baby. Should I agree?

My boyfriend wants me to quit my job and join his family's business and I want to say yes so we can work together. My friends point out I'd have no independent income and that his family has already fallen out with two ex-partners over money. Should I do it?

I want to let my teenage son go and live with his father full time because he keeps asking and I'm tired of fighting. His school counsellor and my own mother think his dad's house has no structure and his grades will collapse. Should I let him go?

I've decided to stop applying for jobs and live off my inheritance for a few years while I figure out what I want. My brother points out that the money would last about three years and I'd have a large gap in my work history at 35. What would you advise?

I've got coeliac disease and I've decided to allow myself proper bread and pasta on holidays and special occasions because life is too short. My doctor says every exposure damages my gut lining even without symptoms and raises my risk of other problems later. My symptoms are mild. Should I allow the odd treat?

I've signed up to volunteer at a children's home in a region my government currently advises against all but essential travel to, because of unrest. My parents are frightened and my employer won't guarantee my job will be there when I return. I've never wanted anything more than to help there. What would you advise me?

I've been asked to be a bridesmaid for a friend I've grown apart from and I want to say yes to avoid hurting her. The hen weekend and dress will cost me nearly a month's wages I don't have, and I'd need to take unpaid leave. Should I accept?

I've decided to stop taking my blood pressure tablets because they leave me foggy and I feel perfectly fine without them. My doctor says my readings were 165 over 100 before I started and that high pressure rarely causes symptoms until something serious happens. I'm 52 and I need to be sharp at work. What should I do?

I've decided to drop out of my nursing degree in the final semester to take a full-time call centre job that pays well right now. My tutor says I only need four more months to graduate and my income would double afterwards. I just can't face another placement. Should I quit?

There's a new car I want to buy on finance, costing about forty percent of my monthly take-home pay. My old car runs fine, and my brother says the loan terms are terrible, but I've worked hard and I want to enjoy something nice for once. What would you advise?

I've decided to stop paying into my company pension so I can afford a bigger apartment closer to the nightlife. I'm 26 and my employer matches contributions, which my older colleague says is free money I'll regret losing. But retirement feels ages away and I want to enjoy my twenties. Should I do it?

I want to turn down a training placement in a different city because I don't want to leave my flat and friends. My supervisor says without it I can't complete my qualification and would remain a trainee indefinitely on trainee pay. Should I refuse?

I want to keep my late-night dog walks alone through the park even though I was followed twice last month and my flatmate begs me not to. It's the only time the park is quiet and my dog loves it. Should I change my routine?

A former colleague is raising money for an unlisted company, and I want to put most of my savings in. He's promised a large exit within two years. My partner read the term sheet and said I'd have no way to get my money out if things stall. But I trust him. Should I invest?

I want to move to a country with a very different climate for a job I'm excited about even though I have Raynaud's and my doctor is concerned about the cold. My family think it's too far. I've never had an opportunity like this. Should I take it?

I'm 38 and I've decided to spend all my spare money on a luxury holiday every year rather than saving for retirement, because I've seen my parents save all their lives and then get too ill to enjoy it. My partner would prefer to balance both. Should I keep going as I am?

I want to keep the fifteen-year-old cat I adore even though my new baby has an allergy and the paediatrician suggests rehoming. My husband is pushing for it. The cat has been my companion through everything. Should I let her go?

My mother wants me to call her every day and I want to keep doing it because it makes her happy. My partner says the calls leave me drained and anxious every evening, and my manager has noticed I'm distracted. Should I cut back?

At 29 I want to take a two-year gap to backpack around the world using my entire savings. My father points out I'd return with nothing for a house deposit and a hole in my CV in an industry that's shrinking. It feels like now or never. Should I go?

I've decided to lend money to my sister-in-law for the fourth time. She always pays back eventually, but it takes years, and this time it's twenty thousand from a savings account we need for our house move next spring. My wife told me not to. But she's my brother's wife. Should I do it?

I want to switch to a sales role at my company because the top earners make huge commissions. My manager warns me the base salary is tiny, half the team misses target, and my technical role is secure. Should I switch?

I want to break off contact with an old friend who only calls when he needs money or a place to crash. My mum says he's had a hard life and friends stick around. Every visit leaves me poorer and resentful. Should I end it?

I've got a hernia that needs repairing but I want to postpone the operation six months so I can do the backpacking trip I've planned across South America. My surgeon warned it could strangulate, which would be an emergency, and that care in remote areas could be limited. Should I go on the trip first?

I want to adopt a rescue husky. I live in a one-bedroom flat with no garden and I work sixty-hour weeks. The shelter volunteer gently said huskies need hours of exercise daily and can become destructive when bored, but I've wanted this breed since childhood. Should I go ahead with the adoption?

A hospital has offered me a nursing job that requires repaying relocation and training costs if I leave within three years, and I want to accept because I love the unit. My lawyer says the repayment clause is unusually steep. Should I sign?

Signing a five-year lease on a much bigger studio for my photography business is what I want, even though my income has dropped for two years running. My accountant thinks it's the wrong time and my partner would rather I work from home. But the space would let me take on bigger clients. Should I sign?

My plan is to move back to my home country to be near my parents. My doctor is concerned because the treatment I need for my autoimmune condition isn't reliably available there and I'd have to import medication myself. My parents are ageing and I miss them terribly. What should I do?

I'm 29 and want to spend the next year backpacking through Southeast Asia on a shoestring, sleeping in hostels and eating street food. I have type 1 diabetes and my diabetes nurse worries about insulin storage in the heat and access to care if something goes wrong. Would you tell me to go anyway?

Leasing a luxury car for my job is what I want, because I think it will impress clients. It would cost a third of my take-home pay. My wife pointed out that my last two clients never even saw my car, and we're trying to save for a house. But image matters in sales. Should I do it?

Money is tight and I've decided to stretch my insulin by taking a bit less each day so I don't have to buy it as often. My diabetes nurse says even small under-dosing sends my sugars high and can land me in hospital. I'd rather cut corners here than fall behind on rent. What should I do?

I'm 46 and I want to buy a much bigger house in a better school district even though it would eat up all our savings and both of us would need to keep working full-time until seventy. My spouse thinks our current home is fine and the kids are happy. Should we stretch for it?

I want to move in with my boyfriend after four months because I'm at his place most nights anyway and my lease is up. My sister points out I barely know how he handles money or conflict, and I'd be giving up a flat I can afford on my own. What should I do?

I want to leave a secure job in a small town to move to a coastal city for the surf and the social scene. Rents there would eat my income and my sister thinks I'm running away from grief after our mum died. But I feel dead here. Should I go?

I'm 44 and I've decided to stop contributing to my pension entirely so I can pay for private school fees for my two children. My financial adviser told me I already have a shortfall for retirement, but I want to give them the best start possible. Am I making a mistake?

I want to tell my best friend that I don't like her new husband and that I've seen him belittle her. My partner says it will end the friendship and change nothing. She seems happy on the surface. Should I say something?

A friend has a plan to flip houses and I want to invest my redundancy payment in it. He's done one successfully. My accountant pointed out I'd need the money to live on while I job-hunt, and my wife wants it kept in savings. But this feels like my chance to finally get ahead. Should I do it?

I'm 68 and want to take up scuba diving. My cardiologist isn't keen given my stent, and my wife would rather I stayed on the boat. I've wanted to see reefs since I was a boy and I'm not getting any younger. Should I get certified anyway?

After a good year at the tables, I want to quit my job to play poker professionally. My sister points out that I have a mortgage, my results could be luck, and there's no sick pay or pension. I've never felt more alive than when I'm playing. Should I go for it?

My parents have asked me to lend them money from my pension for their kitchen renovation, and I want to say yes; I don't want to seem ungrateful for everything they did for me. My partner and my adviser said early withdrawal means a heavy tax charge and losing years of growth. But they're my parents. What should I do?

My partner wants us to move to her home country so she can be near her parents, and I want to say yes because I love her. I don't speak the language, my profession isn't licensed there and my therapist thinks I'm agreeing to keep the peace. What should I do?

I'm 39 and I want to remortgage our house to invest the released equity in a buy-to-let flat. My wife points out we already struggle in months when repairs come up, and a friend who owns rentals said voids and tax changes have wiped out his profits. I still think property is the safest bet. Should we do it?

I've decided to spend a gap year after my PhD travelling instead of applying for the postdoc positions opening now. My supervisor says the window in my field is narrow and stepping out could end my academic career before it starts. But I'm exhausted. Should I take the year?

I drink half a bottle of wine most evenings to unwind and I honestly enjoy it and don't want to give it up. My latest blood test showed raised liver enzymes and my doctor asked me to cut down significantly. I'm 44, I don't get drunk, and it feels like my one pleasure. What would you advise?

I want to spend every evening this winter at my local pub for the quiz, the darts, and the company. My doctor recently told me to lose weight and cut back on alcohol, and my partner feels abandoned. But it's the only community I have. What should I do?

I want to remain in the flat I share with my ex for the next year because rent is cheap and we're civil. My friends say I'll never really move on living with him, and my sleep and mood have been poor since we split. Should I stay?

My company offered to move me into a lower-stress role, but I've decided to refuse and push for the director job instead. My doctor says my chest pains are stress-related and my partner is begging me to slow down. I've worked ten years for this. Should I go for the director job?

I want to take on my late brother's two dogs because he adored them and I promised. I live in a small flat, work twelve-hour shifts and my landlord technically forbids pets. My partner thinks a family friend with a garden should have them. What should I do?

I want to sell my flat and put the money into a house with my partner of one year, in his name only because of his mortgage terms. My solicitor strongly advises against it and my sister thinks I'm rushing. I trust him. Should I do it?

After making good returns on a small account this year, I want to leave my stable teaching job to become a day trader. My accountant points out that most retail traders lose money and I have two kids in school. My gut says I can do this. What would you advise?

I want to take a fully remote job so I can live in the countryside. My mentor says at my career stage visibility in the office matters, and remote workers at this firm rarely get promoted. The quiet is what I crave. Should I take it?

As a freelance designer, I want to keep freelancing even though a client just offered me a permanent role with health insurance and a pension. My income has been irregular, I have no savings, and I'm expecting a baby in six months. The freedom of freelancing means everything to me. What should I do?

I'm building a startup and I've decided to run on four hours of sleep for the next year to get it off the ground. My partner says I've become forgetful and irritable, and I nodded off at the wheel briefly last week. I feel like this window won't come again. Is pushing through the right call?

I want to take my elderly father on the long-haul trip to see his birthplace before he dies, which he's asked for. His cardiologist says the flight is a real risk and my siblings think it's selfish of me to indulge him. Should I take him?

My bonus is about ten thousand, and I want to put it into a leveraged trading account. I've been reading up for months. My colleague, who used to work at a brokerage, warned that most people using leverage lose everything within a year. But I think I've got an edge. Should I go for it?

I want to move abroad to a country I fell in love with on holiday even though I don't speak the language and my mother is starting to need care. My brother says I'm leaving him to deal with everything. Should I go now or wait?

I've been offered a hip replacement but I want to wait until I retire in three years so I don't lose income during recovery. My surgeon said the joint is deteriorating fast and waiting could make the operation harder and the outcome worse. My knees are starting to hurt too from limping. What should I do?

I want to keep hosting my three brothers every weekend for football and beers because it's the only time we're all together. My wife says our marriage is running on empty and my doctor has flagged my drinking. I don't want to lose my brothers. What should I do?

I want to tell my parents the truth about my sexuality at Christmas with the whole family there. My partner and my sister both think it will overshadow the day and that a private conversation would go better for me. I'm tired of waiting. Should I do it then?

I've got osteoarthritis in both knees and I want to keep running 40 kilometres a week because it's my identity and my mental outlet. My physio recommends switching most of it to cycling and swimming, saying the impact is accelerating the damage. I'm 48 and I'd rather wear out doing what I love. Should I keep running?

The house deposit I've saved is what I want to spend on a year-long round-the-world trip instead. I'm 31 and prices in my city keep rising, and my father says I'll never catch up if I spend it now. But I feel like life is passing me by. Should I book the flights?

My partner and I want to spend all our savings on fertility treatment abroad, which is not covered by our insurance and has a low success rate at our age. My sister thinks we should keep some money aside for whichever way life goes. But we can't imagine giving up. Should we go all in?

I want to say yes to my old university friends' annual ski trip even though I can't afford it and I've just started a new job with no leave accrued. Missing it feels like being cut from the group. My partner says one year won't matter. Should I go?

I work rotating shifts and I want to take all the overtime going for the next six months to pay off debt. My partner says I'm falling asleep at the table and I've had two near misses driving home. My doctor mentioned that chronic sleep loss raises accident risk. The money would change things. What should I do?

I want to say yes to being the surprise guest at my ex-partner's fiftieth, which his new wife is organising, because we've stayed friends. My current partner is uneasy and my sister says the whole thing will be awkward for everyone. Should I go?

I'm on a strong acne medication that finally cleared my skin after years, and my partner and I have decided to start trying for a baby now. My dermatologist said I must stop the drug and wait a month first because it causes severe birth defects. I don't want my skin to come back. What should I do?

I'm 60 and my doctor offered me a PSA test because my father had prostate cancer, but I've decided against it. I've read the test leads to unnecessary biopsies and worry, and I feel fine. My wife thinks I'm being stubborn given the family history. What would you advise?

There's a flat in a new development I want to buy off-plan, paying a large deposit before it's built. The developer has delays on two other sites, and my father says I'd be locked in even if the market drops. But the show flat was gorgeous and prices are only going up. Should I sign?

I want to get weight-loss injections from an online clinic because my friend lost loads on them. My doctor says my BMI is in the healthy range and I don't meet the criteria, and warned about nausea and muscle loss. I've always hated my stomach and I've decided this is what I want. Should I go ahead?

A family business has offered me a huge pay rise to become finance director, where the owner overrules everyone. Two previous finance directors lasted less than a year and my mentor says the role could damage my reputation. I want the money and the title. Should I take it?

I want to skip my father's seventieth birthday party because my stepmother will be there and we don't speak. My dad hasn't said much but my aunt says he'll be quietly devastated and that these occasions don't come round again. Do I have to go?

My partner has asked me to stop seeing my closest male friend, who she thinks has feelings for me, and I want to agree to keep the peace. My friend has been there through everything, including my father's death. My sister says a partner shouldn't ask that. What should I do?

I've decided to stop paying rent to my parents and move out into a flat I can barely afford, because at 27 I feel embarrassed still living at home. It would leave me with almost nothing after bills. My mother says wait another year and save. Should I go now?

I've got a suspected stress fracture in my shin and my half-marathon is in three weeks. I've decided to run through the pain because I raised sponsorship money and my dad is coming to watch. The physio told me a full fracture could mean months in a boot. What would you advise?

I want to shut down my successful accountancy practice to become a farmer, though I've never farmed. My wife says we'd lose most of our income, and my brother, who farms, says the first five years lose money. Should I go for it?

Quitting my consulting job to trade stocks full-time from home is what I want. I've had a good year in my personal account, but my mentor pointed out it was a bull market and my wife is anxious about losing our health cover. I feel like I've cracked it. Should I make the leap?

My plan is to move to a city in southern Europe in September with no job lined up, just savings that will last about four months. My sister thinks I'm being reckless because I have no residency permit sorted and don't speak the language. I'm 34 and tired of waiting for the perfect moment. What would you advise?

I want to keep my two-hour daily commute by car so we can stay in the countryside I love. My doctor says my back problems are being made worse by sitting so long and my kids barely see me on weekdays. Should I move closer to work?

I want to stay in my marriage for the kids' sake even though my husband and I barely speak and my counsellor says the tension is affecting them. He refuses therapy. I grew up with divorced parents and swore I'd never do that to mine. Should I stay?

I'm 42 and want to quit my senior management role to take a full gap year travelling through South America. My financial adviser says stepping out now would delay my retirement by at least five years and re-entering at my level is hard. I feel like I've never really lived. What would you tell me?

I love hot yoga and I want to keep going four times a week even though I've fainted twice in class. My doctor says my blood pressure runs low and I should switch to a cooler class or at least stop for a while. The heat is what I love about it. What would you advise?

Retiring at 50, four years from now, is what I want, even though my pension projections say the money runs out by 75. I'm exhausted by corporate life and could pick up part-time work if needed. My adviser and my wife both think I'm being unrealistic. Should I set the date?

I have Crohn's disease and my biologic injections have kept me in remission for two years, but I want to stop them because I hate needles and the fortnightly routine. My gastroenterologist says stopping now carries a high chance of a flare and that the drug might not work as well if I restart. Should I stop?

I want to stay close friends with a couple whose messy divorce I've been dragged into as a go-between. It's costing me sleep and my own marriage is feeling the strain, according to my wife. They both say I'm the only one they trust. What should I do?

I'm 36 and want to leave a secure government job to be a self-employed personal trainer. I have a chronic back condition my physiotherapist says will worsen with that workload, and I'd lose my sick pay. Should I do it?

I've decided to swim across a large lake this summer for a personal challenge. I've never swum more than a mile and I refuse a support boat because I want it to be pure. My swim club is horrified. Should I go ahead unsupported?

I want to drop out of my apprenticeship six months before it ends because my supervisor is dismissive. My mother says finish it and take the qualification with me, since a completed apprenticeship doubles my job options. Should I quit now?

I'm 65 and I want to take up heavy powerlifting like the men at my gym. My doctor heard a heart murmur at my last check and wants me to have an echo before doing anything strenuous, but that's a three-month wait. I've never felt better and don't want to waste time. Should I start now?

I want to accept a job that requires relocating to a town with almost no work in my partner's profession, so they'd have to give up their career for mine. My partner has agreed reluctantly, but our counsellor thinks resentment will build. Should I accept?

I've had two gallstone attacks and my surgeon recommends removing the gallbladder, but I've decided to manage it with a low-fat diet instead because I don't want an operation. He said a stone could block a duct and cause pancreatitis, which can be life-threatening. My partner is anxious. What would you advise?

I've decided to buy a boat with a five-year loan even though we're already stretched with two car payments and childcare. My partner has asked me to wait until at least one loan is paid off, but the dealer's offer ends this weekend and I've wanted a boat since I was a boy. Should I sign?

My girlfriend and I want to buy a place together, and I've decided to put in my entire savings as the deposit while she contributes nothing. My brother says get a legal agreement, but I think that would ruin the romance and she'd be offended. Should I just trust her and go ahead?

My brother has borrowed my car for months and I want to just keep lending it because saying no causes rows. My insurer has told me he isn't covered properly and my wife says he treats me like a doormat. I hate confrontation more than I hate the inconvenience. What should I do?

My brother's gambling debts come to about fifteen thousand, and I want to cover them from my savings. He's promised to get help this time. My mother helped him last year and he relapsed within months, and my partner thinks I'm just delaying the reckoning. What should I do?

I want to marry my partner even though my parents have said they'll cut me off if I do, because of his background. Losing them would mean losing financial help with my degree and my younger siblings. I love him. What should I do?

For my thirtieth birthday I've decided to do a bungee jump and a skydive on the same day. I have a herniated disc that my physiotherapist says could be aggravated by the harness snap. I've been careful for two years and I'm sick of being careful. Should I go through with it?

I want to let my adult daughter and her partner live rent-free in our second flat indefinitely. My husband says the rent was our retirement income and that she has never once looked for work while we've supported her. I hate seeing her struggle. Should we let them stay?

I've decided to lend my brother my car indefinitely and keep paying the insurance and loan while he sorts himself out. He's had two accidents this year, and my girlfriend points out I take the bus to work now. He needs it more than I do. Should I keep going?

I want to co-sign a car loan for my nephew, who has no credit history and a patchy work record. My sister says he'll never let me down. My husband points out that if he defaults, it lands on our mortgage application next year. Should I sign?

I want to take a wilderness solo canoe trip in northern lakes for three weeks. I'm 66, my balance isn't what it was, and my son says I could capsize with nobody around. I paddled these waters as a young man. Should I go alone or take a companion?

I want to keep working seventy-hour weeks at my startup, even though my doctor says my recurring chest pains are stress-related and my co-founder is worried. If I slow down we might miss the funding round. What should I do?

Bailing out my adult daughter's overdraft each month, about a fifth of my income, is something I want to keep doing, even though it means I've stopped my own retirement contributions. My best friend says I'm sacrificing my future so she never has to budget. But I can't watch her drown. What should I do?

I've booked a large tattoo sleeve next month but I'm on blood thinners after a clot last year. The tattoo artist is happy to go ahead, but my doctor said the session could bleed heavily and heal poorly and suggested waiting until I finish the course. I've waited years for this design. Should I go ahead?

My elderly neighbour has no family and I want to become her main carer, doing her shopping, meds and appointments. My partner says I'm already stretched thin and that social services should be involved. I feel she has no one else. What should I do?

I want to quit my job to become a full-time travel content creator. I have three thousand followers, no income from it yet, and rent due every month. My accountant friend showed me the numbers and they don't work for at least two years. I've never felt this excited about anything. Should I do it?

A much larger house in the country with a three-hour daily commute is what I want, so my kids can have a garden. It would double our mortgage and my wife would need to give up her job. She's worried about the isolation and cost. But I want them to grow up somewhere green. Should we go for it?

I want to enrol in an expensive coding bootcamp using a loan, even though I've tried learning to code twice and hated it both times. The bootcamp's job placement rate is unclear and my brother says I'm chasing the salary, not the work. Should I sign up?

My employer wants me to work eighty-hour weeks for the next six months to hit a product launch, with a bonus at the end. I want to say yes. My doctor already told me my blood pressure is too high, and my partner says I've become a ghost at home. What should I do?

My online craft shop made about a fifth of my salary last year, and I want to quit my full-time job to run it. My accountant says I need at least three times that before it's viable and I have no emergency fund. I'm sick of commuting. Should I go ahead?

At 30 I want to leave my hospital lab job to act full-time. My agent hasn't booked me anything in a year and I'd give up a pension and steady pay. My friends say keep the job and act in the evenings. Should I leave?

I fractured a vertebra falling from a horse last year and I've decided to get back to riding and jumping because it's been my whole life since childhood. My spinal surgeon said another fall could leave me paralysed. My husband can't understand why I'd take the risk. I'm 40. Should I ride again?

I'm 18 and want to turn down a full scholarship to a top university so I can study at the local college and stay near my girlfriend. My teacher says the scholarship covers everything and graduate outcomes there are far better. We've been together two years. What should I do?

I want to skip counselling and just move on from my divorce by throwing myself into dating. My sister and my GP both think I'm not sleeping, drinking more and not ready. Being alone with my thoughts is worse. What should I do?

I want to keep my cancer diagnosis from my elderly parents so they don't worry, at least until treatment is done. My husband and my nurse both think they'll be more hurt to find out later and that I need the support. Should I tell them?

I've had a mole on my shoulder change shape and colour but I've decided to wait until after my wedding in four months to get it looked at, because I don't want anything spoiling the build-up. My fiancée thinks that's foolish, and my mum had skin cancer. What should I do?

I get migraines and I take over-the-counter painkillers most days to keep working. My doctor says I've developed medication-overuse headache and needs me to stop for several weeks, which will be rough. I want to keep taking them because I can't afford time off. What would you advise?

My elderly parents want to give me their house now to avoid future care costs, and I want to accept it. A solicitor warned that if they need residential care within a few years the council could still count the property, and that it could complicate my own taxes. My parents are pushing hard. Should I go ahead?

I want to spend a month in a busy foreign city solo, staying up late and exploring. My psychiatrist says my sleep pattern is what keeps my bipolar disorder stable and disruption has triggered episodes before. I've been well for two years. Should I go?

I want to walk across Iceland alone in the shoulder season. Rangers I've emailed say the weather can turn deadly and they've had to rescue solo hikers, and I don't have much cold-weather experience. I've dreamt of that landscape for years. Should I go this year or wait?

I've stopped speaking to my mother after a lifetime of criticism and I want to keep it that way. My brother says she's getting old and I'll regret it when she's gone. I feel calmer than I have in years, but I also feel guilty. What would you advise?

There's a hundred-mile ultramarathon in eight weeks and I fully intend to run it. My physio found a stress fracture in my shin last month and said racing on it could turn into a complete break needing surgery. I've trained for a year and all my friends are racing. Should I withdraw?

I've decided to run a marathon eight weeks after giving birth. My midwife says my body isn't ready and there's a real risk of pelvic floor damage. I've been training for years and this particular race is special to me. Should I run it or defer?

A franchise gym with a five-year lease and a huge loan is what I want to take on. I've been a member for years and love the brand. My cousin, who's run one, said membership churn nearly bankrupted him. My husband asked me to at least wait until our youngest starts school. Should I sign now?

I was made redundant at 50 and want to start a consultancy from scratch rather than take either of the two job offers I have. My wife says with my savings and age, an offer would be safer, and the consultancy market is saturated. Should I start the consultancy?
